notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Georgia

Preparation Grant for Georgia Water Supply, Sanitation, Wastewater, and Hazardous Waste Project

Grant Number: P518850

Assignment Title: Preparation of an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment and Associated Environmental and Social Instruments for the Proposed Hazardous Waste Treatment and Landfill Facility in Georgia

Reference No.: GFPP /CS/CQS-02

The Government of Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Preparation Grant for Georgia Water Supply, Sanitation, Wastewater, and Hazardous Waste Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise preparation of an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and associated environmental and social instruments for the hazardous waste management facilities proposed under the Feasibility Study (FS). These may include pre-treatment facilities (for example, segregation, dewatering and conditioning of oily sludges, contaminated soils and chemical residues); treatment facilities (such as physico-chemical treatment, neutralization and stabilization/solidification, thermal treatment); an engineered hazardous waste landfill; and associated storage, regional waste acceptance and temporary storage facilities, access roads, utilities and transport interfaces, as confirmed through the FS and agreed project scope. The main facility may be located near Marneuli, Kvemo Kartli, Georgia, at the site previously assessed for a non-hazardous waste (municipal) landfill, subject to confirmation. Building on the FS, the 2016 municipal landfill ESIA and available studies, the Consultant will undertake inception and scoping, review and validate existing information, identify data gaps and carry out targeted environmental and social baseline surveys and sampling; assess Georgian environmental assessment, screening, registration and permitting requirements for each relevant facility, alongside applicable World Bank Environmental and Social Standards and EHS Guidelines; describe reasonable alternatives considered in the FS and assess the preferred configuration without repeating technical selection or conceptual design; assess construction, operational, closure and post-closure impacts, including groundwater and soil contamination, emissions, effluents and leachate, hazardous waste handling and transport, worker and community health and safety, credible accidents, emergency preparedness, and climate and natural-hazard risks; undertake stakeholder engagement and disclosure; prepare a detailed, costed Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) and agreed additional instruments (in particular, Stakeholder Engagement Plan and Labor Management Procedures); and support statutory scoping, consultation and regulatory review. The ESIA will be coordinated with the FS and engineering teams and will address regional storage and acceptance facilities to the extent required by their confirmed activities, capacities and applicable regulatory pathways.

The indicative implementation period is approximately 14 weeks from commencement, plus mandatory statutory review and consultation periods, where applicable. The expected start date is [TO BE CONFIRMED]. Estimated level of effort (professional staff-months): [TO BE CONFIRMED]. The schedule will be coordinated with the availability of FS outputs and applicable regulatory procedures.

The Project seeks to enhance the sustainability, resilience, and competitiveness of Zambia's tourism sector while promoting inclusive economic opportunities and conservation outcomes in tourism destinations.

The GREAT-TDP comprises three components:

The People's Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Development of Turtle Hatchery for conservation for the ultimate objective of this assignment is to facilitate hatchling production for conservation of sea turtles in Sonapara, Cox’s Bazar.

  1. The broad scope of consulting services (“the Services”) includes but not limited to:
  • Inception
  • Situational Report
  • Mid-Term Progress Report
  • Comprehensive Conservation Strategy Report
  • The final report consolidating all Deliverables

 

  1. Objectives

The ultimate objective of this assignment is to facilitate hatchling production for conservation of sea turtles in Sonapara, Cox’s Bazar. The specific objectives are to: (1) understand sea turtle nesting sites’ current situation, threats, and necessary conservation actions in Sonapara; (2) establish and operationalize turtle hatchery; and (3) conduct awareness raising activities.

 

  1. Scope of Work
  1. Conduct an assessment and year-round monitoring of sea turtle nesting at Sonapara Beach

The Consultant will identify and map sea turtle nesting sites and conduct focus group discussions (FGDs) with fishers to identify threats (including bycatch, predation, human disturbance, and habitat degradation). The Consultant will monitor nesting throughout the year to capture seasonal patterns and inform conservation actions. Develop a situational report which will cover: (i) identification and characterization of critical nesting habitats; (ii) migration and population studies using appropriate, ethical methods; (iii) development of an inventory of nesting events and hatching success; (iv) documentation of mortality, nesting frequency, and nest fate; and (v) identification and quantification of sources and levels of threats (including bycatch). The Consultant will prepare a comprehensive conservation strategy report summarizing findings and proposing a Conservation Management Plan (CMP) with actionable, long-term strategies, responsibilities, and a time-bound implementation schedule. The report also summarizes the results of all the activities conducted under this assignment.

 

  1. Establish and manage turtle hatchery

The Consultant will establish a turtle hatchery and guard shed with appropriate equipment and security measures. Nests will be managed for safe in-situ incubation and hatching; where in-situ protection is not feasible, the Consultant will implement ex-situ conservation (egg relocation) following accepted protocols and required permits. The Consultant will deploy guards as needed, control predators (e.g., dogs, crows, and other predatory animals), and prevent egg poaching consistent with legal and ethical standards. The Consultant will maintain records of nests managed, relocation activities, hatching success, and predator control actions.

 

  1. Conduct awareness raising activities

The Consultant will conduct awareness meetings with fisher communities on safe handling and release of entangled turtles. The Consultant will identify turtle egg collectors and hold dialogue with them to reduce poaching and promote stewardship. The Consultant will prepare and post informational signboards at key locations, develop and print a sea turtle information poster or leaflet (1,000 copies), and organize media campaigns around turtle hatchling releases and relevant observances (e.g., World Sea Turtle Day), in coordination with local authorities and community groups.

title: The selection of Siraj Product Manager
project_name: Jordan: Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Operation
notice_text:
Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development

Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program

Terms of reference for Siraj Product Manager

Reference No.: JO-MOE-581318-CS-INDV

Program Background:

The Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program for Results (PforR) is a transformative, system-wide reform initiative anchored in Jordan’s Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education.

The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components:

  • Program-for-Results (PforR): the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities.
  • Investment Project Financing (IPF): a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs).

MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms:  

  • RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan.
  • RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. This is complemented by the operationalization of an equivalency system that supports the portability and recognition of TVET qualifications, and enhanced use of learner trajectory data to inform student support services.
  • RA3: Strengthening Sector Governance and Efficiency. The program supports the operationalization of a restructured governance model for the education sector and introduces reforms to human resource management, with a particular focus on teacher recruitment, deployment, and professional development policies.
  • RA4: Digital Transformation in Education, to be introduced through the MASAR Additional Financing (AF), supporting digital and AI-enabled learning for students in Grades 4-12 and strengthening the institutional infrastructure needed for national-scale technology integration in education.

In addition to its core education objectives, MASAR embeds environmental and social sustainability principles across its implementation.

Ultimately, MASAR is designed to deliver measurable, inclusive, and sustainable improvements in Jordan’s education system. It expands access to early learning, strengthens foundational skills, improves graduate employability, strengthens digital skills, technology-enabled learning, and future-ready competencies, and reinforces institutional coherence through evidence-based policymaking. By supporting inclusive education and strengthening school-to-work transitions, the program directly contributes to Jordan’s long-term economic resilience and human capital development agenda.

Objectives of the Assignment:

Siraj is a curriculum-aligned AI learning platform supporting Jordanian classrooms. Siraj Product Manager is accountable for the end-to-end product vision and roadmap, ensuring Siraj delivers measurable learning value, operates with strong safeguarding appropriate for minors, and scales responsibly in partnership with the Ministry of Education. This role requires a combination of education expertise (learning science, learning experience design, curriculum, assessment) and AI product leadership (LLM behavior, evaluation, safety, and iteration at scale).

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Vision & Roadmap
  • Own Siraj’s multi-quarter roadmap aligned with MoE priorities and classroom realities.
  • Set prioritization principles that balance learning impact, learner engagement, usability, safeguarding, feasibility, and cost.
  • Learning Experience & Curriculum Integrity
  • Define the quality standard for Siraj’s learning support across grades/subjects (e.g., scaffolding, misconception handling, formative guidance, age-appropriate responses).
  • Map and optimize the end-to-end learner journey, ensuring the interface and AI interactions minimize extraneous cognitive load.
  • Maintain curriculum alignment and clear boundaries for what the platform should and should not do.
  • AI Quality, Evaluation, and Release Discipline
  • Establish measurable quality criteria for AI behavior (helpfulness, grounding, appropriateness, consistency, and pedagogical alignment).
  • Implement an evaluation approach that combines automated checks with structured human review, and use it to prevent regressions and guide iteration.
  • Safeguarding, Monitoring, and Incident Response

REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN

Assignment Title: Fit-gap analysis in the field of sustainable development, ESG reporting (SASB, IFRS 1/2), development of a decarbonization program, industrial safety, independent reporting certification, and obtaining an ESG rating

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): UZ-CTSI-1004-CS-QCBS-UTY-PM-05

The Republic of Uzbekistan has applied for financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) of the World Bank Group toward the cost of the Connectivity and Transport Sector Improvement Project (CTSIP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the enhancement of the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices of JSC “O‘zbekiston temir yo‘llari” and its Group entities, comprising a Double Materiality Assessment (DMA); assessment of sustainability-related financial risks and opportunities, including climate-related physical and transition risks and opportunities; an integrated ESG diagnostic covering governance, strategy, risk management, data and internal controls, and readiness for IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 reporting; targeted implementation of both ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems at three common operational sites, together with capacity transfer and tools for subsequent Group rollout; a Scope 1, Scope 2 and material Scope 3 GHG emissions inventory and an air pollutant emissions assessment for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 reporting years, and development of decarbonization and air pollutant emissions reduction programs; and preparation of a 2025 SASB-aligned Sustainability Report and a 2026 IFRS S1/S2-aligned Sustainability Report, together with strengthening of internal sustainability reporting readiness. The Services also include support for one initial engagement cycle with one ESG rating agency selected and contracted by the Client. The Client shall pay the agency’s fees; the Consultant shall not guarantee a particular rating outcome.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

At least 5 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving the preparation and/or assurance of sustainability reports under SASB, IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards and/or GRI Standards for companies in transport, infrastructure, utilities, energy, extractives, manufacturing or other asset-intensive sectors. 6. At least 3 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving ISO 14001- and/or ISO 45001-aligned management systems. The combined experience shall cover both standards and include practical implementation, procedures and controls, training, internal audits, management review and corrective actions.

Experience providing ESG, sustainability, governance, climate or corporate transformation advice to state-owned enterprises, sovereign holding companies or public-sector entities will be considered a strong advantage. The consulting services (the “Services”) comprise implementation, analytical support and technical support for the State Register of Damaged and Destroyed Property (RDDP or the “Register”). The assignment aims to support the continuous functioning and effective use of the Register and the services implemented on its basis, and to strengthen the Client’s institutional capacity.

The Services cover five principal service areas:

  1. First-line support and service request analysis: receive, register, classify and analyse user requests; resolve routine issues; escalate matters requiring the Registry Administrator (L2) or the Client (L3); track requests through resolution; and identify recurring issues and best practices.
  2. Implementation support: support the roll-out and use of RDDP services and new or updated functionality, update user instructions and collect feedback on implementation.
  3. Knowledge Base: maintain, populate, structure and update the RDDP Knowledge Base, including guidance, frequently asked questions and documented resolution practices.
  4. User training and methodological support: deliver regular training, webinars and consultations; prepare learning materials; and transfer practical knowledge to users and designated MRIT representatives.
  5. Data analytics and dashboards: configure, maintain and develop Power BI dashboards and analytical reports; support data integration, ETL processes and data quality; and transfer dashboards, documentation and configurations to the Client.

The Services are expected to commence upon the contract’s entry into force, and continue until November 30, 2027. The contract duration may be extended by mutual agreement of the parties in the event of an extension of the Project implementation timelines.

The Services shall be provided under a Time-Based contract, with payment based on actual person-hours worked, supported by approved monthly timesheets and Consolidated Reports. Approval is subject to the applicable service levels and reporting requirements specified in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The estimated level of effort is up to 45,360 person-hours. ADDENDUM

This is an addendum to the Procurement Notice ref:- SO-MOTCA-567865-CS-INDV published on 10 November 2026. Please kindly take note of the new submission deadline of November 30th, 2026. All other aspects of the notice remain unchanged.

1.  BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT

The Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (MoTCA) is implementing the Somalia Infrastructure Development for Access and Jobs, Phase 1 (Stairs2Jobs) Project, financed by the World Bank under the Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA). The Project Development Objective (PDO) of Phase 1 is to increase access to resilient infrastructure and infrastructure sector jobs, and to improve the capacity of select institutions.

MoTCA is responsible for the overall management, coordination, supervision, and implementation of all project activities under the Ministry. This includes ensuring the timely implementation of civil works; the procurement of goods, works, and services; and compliance with applicable environmental and social requirements. The Ministry oversees contractors and supervision consultants to ensure that project activities are implemented in accordance with the required technical, quality, environmental, and social standards. It is also responsible for managing project financial activities in coordination with the EAFD, facilitating the timely processing of payments, and preparing periodic work plans, budgets, progress reports, and other required project documentation.

In addition, MoTCA is responsible for implementing the project’s Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), monitoring and evaluating implementation progress and results, addressing implementation challenges, and regularly reporting project performance, progress, and key issues to the World Bank.

To strengthen the effective management, coordination, and implementation of these responsibilities, MoTCA intends to utilise financing under the Stairs2Jobs Project to recruit a Project Coordinator to support the Ministry in the overall coordination and implementation of project activities.

2.  RESPONSIBILITIES

The PIU Project Coordinator for MoTCA will serve as the focal point for coordination and leadership in the effective planning, implementation, and monitoring of all activities under the Stairs2Jobs Project at the MoTCA level. The Project Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing cross-sectoral project activities, ensuring they are implemented in line with approved project objectives, timelines, and budgets. He or she will facilitate coordination and communication among key stakeholders to ensure smooth and efficient project delivery.

All specific duties and responsibilities are detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR), available on the Ministry’s website at https://motca.gov.so, or upon request via in-person submission or email.

3.  SELECTION CRITERIA

The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience, and skills of the candidate, followed by an interview. The required qualifications, experience, and competencies include:

  • A master’s degree in transport or aviation management, engineering, infrastructure management, public administration, business administration, accounting, economics, or another discipline directly relevant to infrastructure project implementation, institutional coordination, or public-sector programme management, from a recognised university.
  • A minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in project management, infrastructure implementation, transport, aviation, or public administration — of which at least four (4) years must be in transportation, aviation, or infrastructure development related roles, preferably within an FCV context and/or on donor-funded projects.
  • Certification in one or more of the following areas will be given preference: Transport Operations or Planning (TPP), Infrastructure Project Management, Consulting Engineering (FIDIC), Air Traffic Control (ATC), Aeronautical Information Management/Services (AIM), Communication, Navigation and Surveillance (CNS), Airport Management, or other relevant technical certifications from recognised institutions.
  • Demonstrated experience working with government ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs), development partners, or multilateral institutions.

4.  REPORTING

The Consultant will report to the Director General of MoTCA and work under the overall guidance of the World Bank Task Team Leaders for the Stairs2Jobs Project.

5.  DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

The MoTCA PIU Project Coordinator shall be contracted for an initial period of one (1) year, renewable subject to a satisfactory performance evaluation by the Ministry, approval by the World Bank, and the availability of project funds.

6.  SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (MoTCA) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must submit the following:

  • A Curriculum Vitae (CV) including three (3) referees.
  • Copies of certificates of academic qualifications.
  • Copy of passport or ID
  • A cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing — Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2025) (the “Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

7.  DEADLINE AND ADDRESS FOR SUBMISSION

Expressions of Interest and CVs must be delivered to the address below — by hand, mail, courier, or email — on or before Monday, 30th November 2026 at 16:00 hours.

Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport and Telecommunication

 

Terms of Reference

 

for

 

Project Manager

 

Micro Small Medium Enterprises (MSME) and Related Technical Assistance
World Bank / NRPB SPEAR Project – Sint Maarten

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Background and context

Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) constitute approximately 95% of all businesses in Sint Maarten and form the backbone of employment, entrepreneurship, and economic resilience. Recognizing their central role, the Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport and Telecommunication (MinTEATT), through the Department of Economy, Transport and Telecommunication (ETT), is undertaking a comprehensive update of four (4) interrelated MSME-related policies, and the MSME institutional strengthening support programs. These two projects are being implemented under The Sustaining Program Effectiveness and Advancing Resilience (SPEAR) Project, funded by the Government of the Netherlands through the Sint Maarten Reconstruction, Recovery, and Resilience Trust Fund (TF) administered through the World Bank and implemented through the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB)[1].   The Sustaining Program Effectiveness and Advancing Resilience (SPEAR) Project is a strategic initiative led by the Government of Sint Maarten and the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB), with support from the Sint Maarten Trust Fund. It aims to enhance the operational effectiveness of recovery efforts and build long-term institutional resilience. The Trust Fund is governed by a tripartite Steering Committee composed of representatives from Sint Maarten, the Netherlands, and the World Bank, which allocates resources to short-, medium-and long-term recovery and capacity-building initiatives.  SPEAR has the following objectives:

  • Enhance the operational capacity and effectiveness of the National Recovery Program Bureau, and
  • Strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of the Government of Sint Maarten to ensure sustainability of investments.

Scope of Work

This task falls within the second component of SPEAR.

  1. A Policy Consultant or firm is engaged to lead the development of four (4) policy documents: These policies form the foundation of Sint Maarten’s MSME business environment. Updating these policies is essential to reflect the current realities, economic conditions, and evolving dynamics of the local business climate—while also anticipating future needs. At the heart of these policy updates is the goal of fostering a supportive, enabling environment in which entrepreneurs and businesses can thrive and operate efficiently. These revisions aim to strike a thoughtful balance between encouraging economic activity and safeguarding the quality of life, ensuring that Sint Maarten remains a safe, vibrant, and sustainable place to live, work, and do business. The policies are:
  1. The National MSME Policy
  2. The Investment and Diversification Policy
  3. The Residential Economic Policy (REP)
  4. The Beach and Vending Policy

The policy revisions are intended to align and update these policies to reflect current day realities on Island. The update is expected to be informed by data-driven strategies including the proposed World Bank Enterprise Survey[2]. Such data along with the revised policy documents are essential to sustaining progress and achieving inclusive economic growth in the vital Medium Micro and Small Enterprise (MSME) sector in Sint Maarten.  Therefore, the updates, will be critical to ensure alignment between these operational aspects, policy development, MinTEATT priorities, and overall GoSXM priorities.

  1. In parallel to the policy revisions, MinTEATT has requested technical assistance from the ongoing Enterprise Support Project (ESP), funded by the same Trust Fund, to support the execution of the operational aspects of MSME programs. This assistance focuses on institutional strengthening of MSME related institutions including the Sint Maarten Entrepreneurship Development Center (SEDC) and the Chamber of Commerce (COCI). The MSME support areas are:  

 

  1. Governance and Oversight Framework: The objective is to strengthen the Ministry’s oversight and governance of MSME support
  2. Monitoring and Evaluation’ (M&E) framework: Development of an M&E framework for MSME support programs.
  3. Standard Operating procedures (SOPs): Establish SOPs for MSME support programs in key aspects to include basic business training, one-on-one business advisory, and business coaching.
  4. Funding mechanisms for MSME support programs.

Terms of reference for these activities are being developed.

Role of the Project Manager

The Project Manager will be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the SPEAR Project policy development and the ESP MSME institutional strengthening support programs components. This responsibility includes coordinating with the Policy Consultant and other Consultants hired through ESP, managing project workflow, coordinating with Min TEATT/ETT, facilitating stakeholder engagement and ensuring compliance with all project requirements.   The Project Manager will also be responsible for overseeing the day-to-day execution of the project process; maintaining project timelines; ensuring compliance with Government of Sint Maarten requirements; and facilitating the successful delivery of all project outputs. In this role, the project manager shall organize and supervise the identification, formulation, approval, implementation and completion of all activities under the component and liaise with the Project Implementation Unit at the Ministry of Finance (SPEAR) and National Recovery Program Bureau (ESP). Functional responsibilities for the role include:

  1. Project Management and Coordination
  2. Communication with Relevant Stakeholders
  3. Reporting and Monitoring and Evaluation
  4. Oversight and Quality Management

Under the supervision of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Finance for overall project coordination and administrative oversight, and of the Ministry of TEATT, through ETT, for policy direction and substantive technical oversight, the Project Manager is expected to perform the following tasks. ETT will guide the policy content, review and validate project outputs, and ensure alignment with the Ministry’s priorities, with final policy approval remaining with the competent authorities:

Project Management and Coordination

  • Oversee the execution of the policy development update process and the development of MSME Support Programs ensuring that activities, deliverables and timelines across both workstreams progress in line with approved plans
  • Coordinate with Policy Consultants to monitor the project’s progress, address challenges, and ensure alignment with project objectives and timelines.
  • Facilitate and participate in regular project meetings with MinTEATT/ETT, NRPB, Ministry of Finance, the Policy Consultant and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Work directly with project counterparts and relevant stakeholders to ensure deliverables fall within the applicable scope and budget. This will involve coordinating with departments within the Government as well as external counterparts, including NRPB, to ensure all aspects of each project are compatible and to clarify specific requirements of each project.
  • Ensure project milestones are achieved on-time and that deliverables meet the required quality standards.
  • Identify and manage project risks, developing mitigation strategies as needed.
  • Manage the project budget, track expenditures and ensure allocated resources are used in accordance with approved plans.
  • Participate as a member of the bid evaluation team during the contracting process.
  • Support the selection of new project staff or consultants as needed.
  • Support the revision process of operational project documents (e.g., project operations manual, procurement plan, and environmental and social management plan), as needed. Participate and/or lead technical meetings with agency counterparts and project participant
  • Regularly supervise and report on project execution progress and budget performance
  • Assist with the preparation of progress reports and actionable information as required by Government to support its reporting commitments to the Council of Ministers, the Trust Fund Steering Committee and the World Bank, as needed.
  • Any other task related to this function that will contribute to the objectives of the project

Communication with Relevant Stakeholders

  • Facilitate communication among government counterparts, NRPB/WB and private sector stakeholders
  • Provide contributions to press releases related to project activities, as needed
  • Consolidate and track feedback and recommendations from stakeholders and develop response matrices with the Policy Consultant.
  • Ensure timely reporting, briefing notes, and updates to the Ministry of Finance and other governing bodies as required.

Reporting and Monitoring and Evaluation

  • Monitor Policy Consultant’s deliverables and work quality, ensuring it adheres to the TOR, timelines and quality standards.

The Ministry of Finance of the Syrian Arab Republic (the “Employer”) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the services of a Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component (Sub-Component 2.2), who will provide high-level strategic leadership and policy direction to the Government of Syria in the design, sequencing, and oversight of the public procurement reform program under the Project, with a view to establishing a modern, transparent, and efficient procurement system aligned with international best practices.

The Technical Lead will lead and coordinate implementation of the procurement reform activities under Sub-Component 2.2 - the new public procurement legal and regulatory framework (replacing the Uniform System of Contracts Law No. 51 (2004)), standard bidding documents, the Single Procurement Portal (SPP), an independent procurement complaints and review system, and the national procurement professionalization and capacity-development program, advising the Ministry of Finance and relevant stakeholders, coordinating with government entities, development partners and the World Bank Task Team, overseeing implementation progress and risk management, and leading the results framework for procurement reform, including key performance indicators and milestones. The assignment will be for an initial period of one (1) year, with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance and project requirements (the contract may be extended to cover the full duration of the Project).

The Technical Lead will work under the overall guidance of the Project Coordinator and the Public Financial Management Reform Coordinating Unit (PFMRCU) within the Ministry of Finance, and will closely coordinate with relevant government entities, the Syria External Assistance Fiduciary Section (SEAFS) and the World Bank Task Team.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Ministry of Finance (through the Public Financial Management Reform Coordinating Unit - PFMRCU) now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms' staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

  1. postgraduate qualifications in procurement, law, public administration, engineering, economics, or a related field, and at least ten (10) years of relevant professional management-focused experience;
  2. proven successful experience in leading and managing technical assistance projects financed by international donors;
  3. experience in public procurement, including demonstrated experience in procurement reform, development of legal and regulatory frameworks, and institutional strengthening (highly desirable);
  4. advanced leadership skills in organizational change and development, with the ability to introduce critical reforms in complex organizational and contextual structures, including in Fragile and Conflict-affected Situations (FCS);
  5. proven experience in coordinating, cooperating and negotiating with high-level government officials, donor partners and multiple local stakeholders; and
  6. fluency in Arabic and English.

 

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers [insert correct title and date of applicable Regulations edition as per the financing agreement] (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Ministry of Finance

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project

Joul Jammal Street, P.O. Box 13136

Damascus, Syrian Arab Republic

E-mail: syriapfmprocurement@gmail.com

 

 

=======================================================================

 

Terms of Reference (TOR)

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516)

Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component

 

Project Background

  1. Syria is making progress in its transition towards stabilization, recovery, and reintegration, while continuing to face major challenges after 14 years of conflict. More than one year after the December 2024 political transition, the new Syrian government under the leadership of President Al-Sharaa has maintained overall political stability. Modest economic growth is projected for 2025 and 2026, and Syria has benefitted from the lifting of major economic sanctions and renewed participation in international financial systems and investment discussions. At the same time, the security situation remains fragile, with occasional outbreaks of violence, and the country faces massive development challenges and continued humanitarian needs. Continued international engagement and financing will be critical to support Syria in its post-conflict transition. 
  2. Sound management of public funds and transparency about their use are prerequisites for the Syrian state to gain the trust of its citizens and the international community as it seeks to mobilize resources and deliver services to the population. Fourteen years of conflict and economic mismanagement have weakened the capacity and legitimacy of Syria’s state institutions. A disciplined and transparent approach to public financial management (PFM) will be a critical foundation for Syria’s path to recovery and development. The Ministry of Finance has identified support for PFM reforms as a priority, highlighting the immediate need to update the relevant legal framework, rebuild human capital for core government functions, advance digitalization, and establish accountability and transparency. Sound management of public funds will also be needed to mobilize external assistance for the country’s massive reconstruction needs, with expectations from the international community of adequate oversight of reconstruction investments, payroll, and the flow of funds to provide these resource flows.
  3. The Syrian Arab Republic has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing for services of a Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component. The project components/sub-components are shown in Table 1. Full details are available in the Project Appraisal Document (PAD).

Table 1: Summary of project components/sub-components

 

  1. Within this context, Component 2 of the Project focuses on improving the efficiency and effectiveness of essential PFM and procurement functions. A key sub-component (Sub-component 2.2) is dedicated to public procurement reform, which aims to establish a modern, transparent, and efficient procurement system aligned with good international practices. This includes the development of a new procurement legal framework, introduction of standard bidding documents, establishment of a Single Procurement Portal (SPP), strengthening of complaint handling mechanisms, and development of procurement professionalization programs.
  2. The current procurement system, governed by the Uniform System of Contracts Law No. 51 (2004), presents several structural gaps and limitations, including weaknesses in competition, transparency, complaints review, and the absence of modern e-procurement systems.

 

Objective of the Assignment

  1. The objective of this assignment is to provide high-level strategic leadership and policy direction to the Government of Syria in the design, sequencing, and oversight of the public procurement reform program under the Project, with a view to establishing a modern, transparent, and efficient procurement system aligned with international best practices.

The Technical Lead will guide the reform agenda at the institutional and policy level, ensure coherence across reform pillars, and support sustainable capacity development and ownership by government institutions.

Tasks and Responsibilities

  1. The Technical Lead for Public Procurement Reform Component will be responsible for leading and coordinating the implementation of the public procurement reform activities under the Project and providing advisory support to the Ministry of Finance and relevant stakeholders.

In particular, the Lead will undertake the following tasks:

  1. Strategic Leadership and Reform Direction:
  • Provide overall vision, leadership, and strategic direction for the public procurement reform program, ensuring alignment with national priorities and international good practices.
  • Define and guide the sequencing and prioritization of reform initiatives, taking into account institutional readiness and the FCV context.
  • Advise senior government leadership on policy options, reform trade-offs, and implementation risks.

 

  1. Procurement Legal and Regulatory Reform:
  • Lead the strategic design and oversight of the new public procurement legal and regulatory framework, ensuring coherence, applicability, and sustainability.
  • Oversee the work of technical teams responsible for drafting legislation and regulations and ensure quality assurance and policy consistency.
  • Facilitate high-level consultations and consensus-building among key stakeholders to support adoption of the reform framework.

 

  1. Digital Transformation and System Modernization
  • Provide strategic guidance on the development and implementation of the Single Procurement Portal (SPP) as a cornerstone for transparency and efficiency.
  • Ensure that digital solutions are aligned with broader public financial management systems and government digital strategies.
  • Oversee high-level design decisions to ensure sustainability, interoperability, and scalability of systems.

 

  1. Complaint Handling and Oversight Mechanisms:
  • Lead the strategic design of an independent and credible procurement complaints and review system.
  • Ensure that oversight mechanisms are aligned with principles of fairness, transparency, and due process, and are institutionally sustainable.

 

  1. Capacity Development and Professionalization Strategy
  • Provide strategic guidance on the development of a national procurement professionalization framework, including certification pathways and institutional arrangements.
  • Oversee the design of capacity development programs to ensure long-term institutional strengthening, rather than short-term training delivery.
  • Promote a culture of professionalism and ethical standards in the procurement function across government.

 

  1. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination
  • Act as a key interlocutor with senior government officials, development partners, and other stakeholders on procurement reform matters.
  • Ensure effective coordination across ministries, agencies, and donor-supported initiatives to avoid fragmentation and duplication.
  • Support the Government in articulating and communicating the reform agenda to build broad-based ownership.

 

  1.  Implementation Oversight and Risk Management
  • Provide strategic oversight of implementation progress, ensuring that reform activities remain aligned with objectives and timelines.
  • Identify key implementation risks and bottlenecks and advise on mitigation measures at the policy and institutional levels.
  • Guide pilot initiatives and scale-up decisions from a strategic perspective.

 

  1. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Results Orientation
  • Lead the development of a results framework for procurement reform, including key performance indicators and milestones.
  • Oversee monitoring and evaluation processes to ensure evidence-based decision-making and adaptive management.
  • Provide high-level reporting and strategic insights to inform the Government and the World Bank on reform progress.

 

Deliverables

  1. The overall deliverable is the successful and timely implementation of the project activities as contained in Sub-Component 2.2 under the project.  The Technical lead will also be expected to achieve smooth, effective, and efficient disbursement of the budget allocated for Sub-Component 2.2. Specific delivery includes work programs, budgets, procurement plan and periodic progress and delivered as they fall due.

 

Duration of the Assignment

  1. The assignment will be for an initial period of one (1) year, with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance and project requirements. The contract may be extended to cover the full duration of the Project.

 

 

Institutional Arrangements

  1. The Technical Lead will work under the overall guidance of the Project Coordinator and the PFM Reform Coordinating Unit (PFMRCU) within the Ministry of Finance and will closely coordinate with relevant government entities, the Syria External Assistance Fiduciary Section (SEAFS), and the World Bank Task Team.

 

Qualification and Experience Requirements

  • The suitable candidate for appointment must hold postgraduate qualifications in procurement, law, public administration, engineering, economics, or a related field, and at least ten (10) years of relevant professional managementfocused experience.

 

  • Proven successful experience in leading and managing Technical Assistance projects financed by international donors.

 

  • Experience in public procurement, including demonstrated experience in procurement reform, development of legal and regulatory frameworks, and institutional strengthening is highly desirable.

 

  • Candidate must possess excellent interpersonal skills, strong oral and written communication skills, problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, with the ability to succeed in evolving Fragile, Conflict, and Violence (FCV) environment. be proficient in the use of the computer.
  • Advance leadership skills in organizational change and development with the ability to introduce critical reforms in complex organizational/contextual structures.
  • Proven experience in coordinating, cooperating and negotiating with high level Government officials, donor partners and multitude of local stakeholders.
  • Excellent Knowledge in International management Standard for Quality management System, Health & Safety Management System, Environmental Management System, Business Continuity Management System, Information Security Management System.
  • Fluent in Arabic and English.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-2.6--4-R – Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

 

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

GPE TF0D0613

 

Assignment Title: Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

No. LEARN-2.6--4-R

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in aligning budget planning and public financial management processes with the strategic priorities of the education sector and the implementation of flagship national programmes and reforms. In particular, the assignment will contribute to the effective planning, prioritisation, financing, and coordination of key initiatives. The Consultant will support the development of effective planning and resource allocation approaches aimed at improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency of public expenditure, strengthening evidence-based decision-making, and ensuring better alignment between strategic objectives, reform implementation, and available financial resources.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest. The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time December 01, 2026.

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for Consulting Services (Individual Consultant)

Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

Contract No. LEARN-2.6-CC-4-R

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project

GPE TF0D0613

I. Background

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln  provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675.9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln.

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, a Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) was signed between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (Loan No. K019-UA) in the amount of $286 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

II. Objective

The objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in aligning budget planning and public financial management processes with the strategic priorities of the education sector and the implementation of flagship national programmes and reforms. In particular, the assignment will contribute to the effective planning, prioritisation, financing, and coordination of key initiatives. The Consultant will support the development of effective planning and resource allocation approaches aimed at improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency of public expenditure, strengthening evidence-based decision-making, and ensuring better alignment between strategic objectives, reform implementation, and available financial resources.

III. Scope of services

The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to:

  • Analyze the current system of budgetary and strategic planning within the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES), including the application of the program-based budgeting approach;
  • Analyze the alignment of budget programs with strategic objectives and national policy priorities in the education and science sector;
  • Develop recommendations for aligning strategic documents (strategies, operational plans) with MoES budget programs;
  • Ensure integration of strategic objectives and priorities into the budget process (including preparation of budget requests, budget program passports, and reporting);
  • Contribute to the improvement of the structure of budget programs, performance indicators, and effectiveness metrics;
  • Support medium-term budget planning in line with strategic documents;
  • Provide methodological support on the application of the program-based budgeting approach within MoES;
  • Coordinate with the Ministry of Finance of Ukraine on budget planning and alignment of budget programs;
  • Provide methodological and analytical support for public expenditure reviews in relevant MoES sectors;
  • Develop proposals for implementing recommendations from expenditure reviews and ensure their incorporation into future budget planning cycles;
  • Support the implementation of results-based management approaches in the budget process;
  • Assess the effectiveness of MoES budget programs;
  • Prepare analytical materials on the efficiency of public expenditure and achievement of results.

Expected Deliverables:

  • Regular reports on the progress of aligning budgetary and strategic planning;
  • Analytical notes on the effectiveness of budget programs and their alignment with strategic objectives;
  • Proposals for improving the MoES budget process:

consulting and practical support to the Ministry of Education and Science in implementing results-oriented management approaches;

conducting analysis and assessment of the efficiency and effectiveness of budget programs of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine;

  • Analyze the implementation of previously provided recommendations and their impact on MoES budget indicators in the medium term, including collection and systematization of recommendations provided by the Accounting Chamber, the State Audit Service, and expenditure reviews conducted during the previous three years, as well as assessment of their implementation status.

 

IV. Reporting

The Consultant shall report to the Project Coordinator/Project Co-Coordinator and work in coordination with the Deputy Ministers of Education and Science of Ukraine, relevant MoES directorates, and project managers involved in the implementation of Project activities. On operational matters, the Consultant shall cooperate with the Head of the World Bank Operations Management Team.

The Consultant shall submit monthly reports to Project coordinator / Project Co-coordinator in hard copy. The reports shall include a description of services provided during the reporting period.

 

V. Provided resources

 

MoES shall provide the Consultant with the information necessary to carry out his/her assignment in a timely manner. MoES may provide the Consultant with a workplace, including necessary equipment to carry out his/her functions (e.g. PC, communications and office equipment).

 

VI.  Qualification requirements

 

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

 

  • Master’s degree or higher in finance, economics, accounting, or taxation;
  • At least 5 years of professional experience in public financial management or related areas;
  • Experience in strategic planning and alignment of budget programmes with sectoral policies.
  • Fluency in Ukrainian;
  • Proficiency in English at a minimum level of B1.

 

Desirable skills and qualifications:

  • Experience in effective communication among different government authorities;
  • Experience working with reforms or policies in the education and/or science sector;
  • Skills in using analytical tools and basic data visualization tools;
  • Experience in drafting regulatory/legal acts;

 

VII.  Period and location of employment

The Consultant shall provide his/her services until October 30, 2027. The contract may be extended subject to satisfactory performance and mutual agreement between the Consultant and the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine during the Project financing period.

The Consultant is expected to provide services under this Agreement on an ongoing basis throughout its term at a level of engagement equivalent to full-time employment, to the extent necessary to properly perform the tasks specified in the Terms of Reference.

The Consultant shall provide services primarily in Kyiv, Ukraine, and may take business trips to other regions of Ukraine to support implementation of the Project.

The Consultant is expected to be able to provide services remotely, but at the MOES request must arrive and/or provide services at the MOES premises as soon as possible.

VIII. Application package

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org, maryna.chubenko@mon.gov.ua indicating the email subject: «LEARN-2.6-CC-4-R: Selection of the Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert 2 (Budget Planning): [NAME]».

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time December 01, 2026.

If the candidate fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the candidate’s application.

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the International Development Association toward the cost of the Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project. “Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC (IT Park), as the Implementing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds to engage an individual consultant as AI and Technology Ecosystem Adviser to the CEO of IT Park Uzbekistan, under Subcomponent 1.1 of the Project.

Under Subcomponent 1.1, the Project supports IT Park Uzbekistan’s AI and technology ecosystem agenda, including the implementation of AI strategy, priority AI initiatives, international technology partnerships and the commercialization of innovations, in line with Uzbekistan’s Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies until 2030.

The Adviser will support the CEO of IT Park in prioritising, designing and delivering
AI ecosystem initiatives, partnerships and programmes, and in strengthening IT Park’s internal capacity to manage its AI agenda. Results are expected to contribute to the Project Development Objective through the creation of digital jobs, growth of AI-enabled IT services exports and inclusion of women, youth, persons with disabilities and the regions.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include, but are not limited to:

  • assessment of existing AI initiatives, capabilities and AI-readiness, and recommendation of priorities for a 12-month AI ecosystem work plan;
  • advice on strategic AI-related decisions, including decision papers on proposed AI programmes, centres, partnerships and investment initiatives;
  • identification and engagement of international technology partners, and support for cooperation proposals and authorised negotiations;
  • support for applied AI initiatives and the commercialisation of innovations developed by local startups and IT Park residents;
  • advice on mechanisms to attract AI talent and strengthen IT Park’s institutional capacity, including working sessions for IT Park staff;
  • support to the CEO across IT Park’s strategic directions (startups and venture investment; export and international positioning; Uzbekistan as a regional technology hub; support to IT Park residents and their AI adaptation; and R&D, data and robotics).

The assignment is proposed for a period of 12 months. The Adviser will work in a hybrid format, under a time-based contract.

To obtain the Terms of Reference for the assignment, please send your request to the following e-mail address: udip@it-park.uz.

“Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services: a curriculum vitae in the English language, and contact details of references.

The evaluation criteria are:

1) General Qualifications

  • University degree in technology, engineering, economics, management or a related field;
  • Fluent professional English;
  • Availability to work in person in Tashkent, Uzbekistan for at least 5 working days per month throughout the assignment.

2) Professional Experience

  • At least 8 years of experience in technology businesses, innovation, digital transformation or technology ecosystem development, including at least 5 years in leadership or strategic roles;
  • At least 3 years of substantive experience in managing AI projects or programmes, and at least one completed AI initiative with verifiable results and a clearly identified personal contribution;
  • Demonstrated experience in advising senior decision-makers, developing programmes involving companies, startups, universities, investors and public institutions, and supporting technologies through pilots, deployment, licensing, investment or entry into overseas markets;
  • Experience in international technology projects, negotiations with organisational leaders and cooperation with government bodies or development institutions;
  • Active professional relationships with AI companies, technology centres, customers and investors, supported by examples of collaboration.

3) Advantages

  • Russian or Uzbek proficiency;
  • Experience with recognised technology clusters or AI centres;
  • Experience working on MDB-financed projects (e.g., World Bank, ADB);
  • Experience in developing or transition economies, preferably in Central Asia/CIS, including AI ecosystem or policy development;
  • Knowledge of responsible AI and data governance frameworks.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest, and to paragraph 3.21 on eligibility.

  1. Background and Rationale

The Government of the Republic of Moldova is implementing the Strengthening Moldova's Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Project (SMORE), financed by the World Bank. The Project aims to strengthen national preparedness and resilience to natural hazards and climate-related shocks, including through improved policy, regulatory and technical instruments for disaster risk reduction.

This assignment is part of Subcomponent 3.1 - which includes technical assistance for the development of methodologies, regulatory documents, data systems and supporting tools aimed at reducing seismic risk in the Republic of Moldova. Within this framework, the methodology for the elaboration of the Interactive Map on Seismic Risk is required as a core technical product linking seismic hazard, exposure and vulnerability information into a coherent and usable risk assessment framework.

The Republic of Moldova is exposed to significant seismic hazard, primarily generated by the Vrancea intermediate-depth seismic source (Romania), which has historically affected the entire territory of the country. The 1940 (M 7.4) and 1977 (M 7.2) earthquakes underlined the vulnerability of the existing building stock and the importance of integrated risk assessment for prioritization of public investment, retrofit planning and emergency preparedness. In this context, an interactive seismic risk map — built on an explicit and reproducible methodology — is a foundational instrument for evidence-based seismic risk management.

    1. Conceptual scope of the interactive seismic risk map

Object of the risk assessment. This Terms of Reference addresses the seismic risk of buildings. The primary risk objects of the methodology and of the interactive map are buildings — residential, public and other categories agreed with the Client — consistent with the PAD, with the RVS methodology under GD 334/2025 (Activity 1b) and with the retrofit feasibility studies under Activity 1d. Critical facilities and infrastructure may be represented as contextual/ancillary layers for interpretation and prioritization (e.g. location of hospitals, schools, emergency services), but the full seismic risk modelling of infrastructure networks (utilities, transport, lifelines) is outside the scope of this assignment, because it requires component-specific fragility models and network data that are not available in the Republic of Moldova and are not covered by the Subcomponent 3.1 data chain

The interactive seismic risk map is not, by design, a mere visualization product. It is the visible output of a structured technical process that must define: the data architecture, the calculation logic, the risk indicators and their thresholds, the treatment of uncertainties, the scenarios to be assessed, and the rules for presenting results in a transparent, auditable and reproducible manner. The map shall enable public authorities, technical experts and decision makers to identify where seismic risk is concentrated, which factors drive that risk, and how alternative assumptions or scenarios affect the outcome.

The assignment is closely coupled with the other outputs of Subcomponent 3.1, in particular: (i) the methodology for seismic hazard zoning developed under Activity 1a, which provides the hazard input layer; (ii) the Rapid Visual Screening (RVS) methodology operationalized through Activity 1b, which provides the building-level exposure and vulnerability data; (iii) the future regulatory NCM package harmonized with Eurocode 8; and (iv) the seismic risk reduction recommendations to be developed under subsequent project activities. The methodology for the interactive risk map shall therefore be designed to be coherent with hazard, exposure and fragility/vulnerability datasets, compatible with GIS-based workflows, and suitable for integration into institutional planning and regulatory-support activities, applying the Common Data Standard and the coordination mechanism defined in Section 3.12.

    1. Boundaries of this assignment

Methodology — not software development. This assignment is preparatory and methodological in nature. It explicitly covers the development of the seismic risk methodology for buildings, the data architecture, the calculation model, indicators and thresholds, the functional specification for the interactive map, and (where feasible within available data) a methodological pilot or demonstrator. It does not include full-scale software/web-GIS development, deployment of a production IT platform, code production, hosting infrastructure, large-scale data acquisition, or final population of the interactive map with the complete national dataset, all of which are foreseen as subsequent activities to be procured under separate contracts.

Accordingly, the critical quality risk under this assignment is not the coding of an interactive web-GIS application, but the correct translation of seismic risk principles, hazard-exposure-fragility/vulnerability integration logic, indicator structure, threshold classification and GIS data architecture into a complete, internally coherent and procurement-ready specification. Where a pilot or demonstrator is included, it shall serve only to test and validate the methodology — not to substitute the future production interactive map system.

In line with the principle of fit-for-purpose expertise, the Key Experts required under this Terms of Reference shall be focused on seismic risk methodology, exposure and fragility/vulnerability modelling, structural and earthquake engineering, and GIS / spatial-data architecture. Given the role of the pilot/demonstrator and of the functional specification, an IT / Web-GIS specialist shall additionally be included in the team as a mandatory non-key expert (Section 7.4), assessed on a responsive basis;IT or web-GIS development input may be mobilized as non-key or short-term support, including through subcontracting or through qualified members of the Consultant's technical team with proven experience in interactive mapping or web-GIS configuration.

This Terms of Reference also includes, as a secondary and framework-level output built on the seismic risk map results, a buildings-focused seismic resilience strategic framework (Section 3.13). This framework is deliberately limited to the building sector and to the strategic (policy and prioritization) level; it is not a full standalone National Seismic Risk Reduction Strategy. The broader themes of institutional arrangements, emergency response, reconstruction planning, financing mechanisms and public communication are identified as follow-on activities rather than developed under this assignment.

    1. Justification and need

The Republic of Moldova currently lacks an integrated, methodologically harmonized and publicly accessible seismic risk mapping framework. Existing seismic hazard maps, building data and disaster risk information are fragmented across institutional sources, are not structured around a common data architecture, and are not yet integrated into a transparent risk-calculation framework usable for policy, investment and emergency preparedness decisions. A robust, traceable and reproducible methodology for the elaboration of an Interactive Seismic Risk Map is therefore a precondition for:

  • the integration of the seismic hazard zoning developed under Activity 1a with the exposure and vulnerability data collected through the RVS process under Activity 1b;
  • the prioritization of public buildings and critical infrastructure for detailed seismic assessment, retrofit feasibility studies and public-investment decisions;
  • the alignment of national practice with recognized international risk-mapping frameworks (GEM, UNDRR, JRC, INFORM Risk, Risk Data Library and equivalent);
  • evidence-based decision making for seismic risk reduction at central, regional and local government levels;
  • transparent, auditable communication of risk to non-specialist audiences while preserving scientific rigour;
  • the preparation of a defensible, technology-neutral procurement of any future interactive map development service, in line with World Bank Procurement Regulations.
    1. Legal and regulatory framework

The services to be carried out under this Terms of Reference shall comply with, but not be limited to, the following legal and regulatory references:

  • Code of Urbanism and Construction No. 434/2023 (Codul Urbanismului i Construciilor) and subsequent implementing acts;
  • Government Decision No. 334 of 05.06.2025 on the Regulation for Rapid Visual Screening (RVS) of existing buildings;
  • NCM A.07.02 — Quality assurance in design and execution of constructions;
  • EN 1998-1:2004 + A1:2013 — Eurocode 8: Design of structures for earthquake resistance — Part 1: General rules, seismic actions and rules for buildings;
  • EN 1998-3:2005 — Eurocode 8 — Part 3: Assessment and retrofitting of buildings;
  • ISO 19115 — Geographic information — Metadata; INSPIRE Directive principles for spatial-data interoperability;
  • OGC standards for web-GIS services (WMS, WFS, WMTS) — to be referenced where relevant for the functional specification;
  • Law No. 133/2011 on the protection of personal data, with subsequent amendments;
  • Law No. 271/1994 on civil protection, and the institutional framework for emergency management in the Republic of Moldova;
  • Reference international frameworks: GEM (Global Earthquake Model) risk methodology, UNDRR/UNISDR risk terminology, JRC INFORM Risk Index, Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030;
  • Recent Romanian national methodology for the development of seismic risk maps and related Ro-Risk outputs (reference regional practice for Vrancea-type intermediate-depth seismicity);
  • World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (current edition);
  • World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) — relevant Environmental and Social Standards;
  • Quality Assurance Plan (QAP) of Subcomponent 3.1 — current approved version.
  1. Objective of the Assignment

The general objective of the assignment is to develop a complete and technically justified methodology for the elaboration of the Interactive Map on Seismic Risk of buildings for the Republic of Moldova, including the conceptual model, data architecture, calculation approach, indicators, threshold intervals, GIS/data requirements and functional specification necessary for practical implementation.

The assignment shall establish how seismic risk is calculated, documented and communicated by combining the three fundamental components of seismic risk: hazard, exposure and fragility/vulnerability. The Consultant shall define the required input data, minimum attributes, spatial units, assumptions, formulas, risk scenarios, uncertainty treatment, classification logic and outputs to be used for the interactive map.

The specific objective is to produce a methodology that can be used by MIRD, OEAPM/PIU, technical reviewers, consultants, public authorities and other designated users as a reliable reference for seismic risk mapping, prioritization and decision support. The methodology shall not be limited to a narrative description; it shall provide practical rules, tables, matrices, data templates and calculation logic that allow the results to be verified and reproduced.

The assignment shall also produce the functional specification for the Interactive Seismic Risk Map. This specification shall describe required layers, filters, tools, comparison of results and scenarios, import/export functions, reporting functions, access modes, performance expectations, scalability, security, auditability and update mechanisms. This shall be prepared as a technical bridge between the seismic risk methodology and any future or parallel IT/web-GIS implementation.

In addition, and building on the outputs above, the assignment shall produce a concise, buildings-focused seismic resilience strategic framework (Section 3.13).
