CONSULTANCY SERVICE TO ASSESS THE ECONOMIC IMPLICATIONS AND PUBLIC PERCEPTIONS OF THE FREE MOVEMENT OF PERSONS PROTOCOL.

 

REF: ET-AUC-569896-CS-QCBS

 

 

  1. Background

The African Union (AU), through Agenda 2063 and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), has positioned regional integration as a cornerstone of Africa’s economic transformation. The Free Movement of Persons (FMP) and labour mobility are critical enablers of this vision, facilitating trade in services, investment, skills mobility, tourism, and the development of regional value chains across the continent.

To advance these objectives, the AU adopted the FMP Protocol in 2018 (African Union, 2018), with the aim of progressively removing barriers to mobility among Member States. Effective implementation of the Protocol is expected to enhance productivity, competitiveness, employment opportunities, and broader economic integration. However, progress towards ratification and implementation has remained limited, largely due to concerns related to security, labour market impacts, migration governance, and national sovereignty. As of September 2026, 32 Member States have signed the Protocol and four (Mali, Niger, Rwanda, and São Tomé and Príncipe) have ratified it, against the 15 ratifications required for entry into force; no new signature or ratification has been recorded since 2019 (ICMPD and AUC, 2025; Mo Ibrahim Foundation, 2026). Existing analytical work has documented the expected benefits of free movement and the reasons for slow ratification (AUC and IOM, 2018; Hirsch, 2021; ECA and AUC, 2023; ICMPD and AUC, 2025), but has not yet quantified the incremental economic effects of the Protocol against a counterfactual, nor the distribution of its costs and benefits across Member States (UNCTAD, 2018; Maskus, 2023).

In contrast, several Regional Economic Communities (RECs), particularly ECOWAS, have implemented the right of entry (Phase 1 of the FMP Protocol) for their citizens, while the rights of residence and establishment remain only partially implemented, and border closures, deportations and re-introduced formalities have at times reversed progress (ECA and AUC, 2023; ICMPD and AUC, 2025; AfDB and AUC, 2025). The differing levels of acceptance and implementation between regional and continental mobility frameworks present an important policy question for the African Union and highlight the need for a better understanding of both the economic opportunities and the socio-political factors influencing support for free movement.

This study is financed under the World Bank-supported Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda 2063 (BIASHARA) project (P180117), which supports the AUC and the AfCFTA Secretariat in advancing three Agenda 2063 flagship commitments – the AfCFTA, the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM) and the FMP Protocol – and which includes performance-based conditions on the alignment of Member State and REC legal and regulatory frameworks with all three instruments (World Bank, 2023). The study is therefore expected to treat the FMP Protocol as one pillar of an integrated market-access, connectivity and mobility agenda, and its outputs will feed the BIASHARA results framework and the AU scorecards on AfCFTA, SAATM and FMP implementation.

Against this backdrop, the African Union Commission (AUC) seeks to undertake a comprehensive study that integrates the following two complementary lines of inquiry:

  1. Phase 1 (economic implications) will assess the prospective economic implications of implementing the FMP Protocol, including its potential impact on trade, tourism, labour markets, investment, and regional economic integration.
  2. Phase 2 (public and stakeholder perceptions) will examine public perceptions of mobility and labour movement across Africa, identifying the factors that shape acceptance, resistance, trust, and concerns regarding regional and continental mobility initiatives. Drawing on comparative regional experiences, observed mobility practices, and selected country case studies, the study will generate evidence-based insights and practical recommendations to support effective implementation of the FMP Protocol and strengthen Africa's regional integration agenda.

The two phases will be delivered by a single consulting firm (or consortium) as parallel workstreams under one inception report, one steering committee and one integrated final report, so that the economic evidence generated in Phase 1 informs the communication and advocacy outputs of Phase 2.

Phase 1: Assessment of the Economic Implications of the Free Movement of Persons Protocol and Comparative Analysis of Regional Mobility Regimes in Africa

This assignment integrates two complementary analytical components:

  • Study A: Assessment of the economic implications of the Free Movement Protocol on trade, tourism, and labour markets (economic impact)
  • Study B: Comparative analysis of regional mobility regimes and exploratory case studies of first-mover countries (comparative analysis)

Together, these analyses will provide practical, evidence-based insights to support AU Member States in advancing the implementation of the FMP Protocol and maximizing its economic benefits.

  1. Objectives of the Assignment

The overall objective of this consultancy is to generate policy-relevant, forward-looking evidence and strategic guidance to support the implementation of the AU Free Movement of Persons (FMP) Protocol.

Specifically, the assignment aims to:

  • Provide a quantified, scenario-based assessment of the incremental economic effects of implementing the FMP Protocol – relative to a baseline of continued unilateral and REC-level visa liberalisation – covering trade, tourism and air travel, labour markets, regional value chains, public finances and broader economic growth, and reporting both benefits and costs.
  • Quantify how benefits and costs are distributed across Member States (countries of origin and destination; income groups; skilled and less-skilled workers; women and men), and identify the fiscal implications for Member States, including visa and permit revenue foregone and the tax and social contributions of mobile workers.
  • Demonstrate the contribution of labour mobility to AfCFTA implementation, particularly in relation to trade in services (Mode 4), productivity, and regional economic integration, and the complementarity between the FMP Protocol, the AfCFTA and the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM).
  • Generate comparative, evidence-based insights from existing regional mobility regimes and first-mover countries, highlighting enabling conditions, practical implementation approaches, and early outcomes, including the reasons why the rights of residence and establishment have lagged behind the right of entry and the lessons of reversal episodes.
  • Deliver actionable, policy-oriented recommendations and strategic guidance to inform:
    • AU policy dialogue and advocacy
    • AfCFTA-aligned economic integration strategies
    • Member States’ implementation of the FMP Protocol
    • BIASHARA programme monitoring and the AU scorecards on AfCFTA, SAATM and FMP implementation
  1.  Scope of Work

The consultant will undertake the following tasks:

  1. Conduct a comprehensive review of literature, policy frameworks, and existing studies on the economic impacts of migration, mobility, and labour movement in Africa, including AfCFTA-related dynamics. The review shall take the existing evidence base as its starting point and state explicitly what the present study adds; at a minimum it shall cover AUC and IOM (2018), UNCTAD (2018), OECD and ILO (2018), World Bank (2020), Hirsch (2021), Bisong (2022), ECA and AUC (2023), Chime et al. (2023), Maskus (2023), IOM and AUC (2024), ICMPD and AUC (2025), ECA and AUC (2025), the Africa Visa Openness Index series (AfDB and AUC, 2025), Mo Ibrahim Foundation (2026) and Afrobarometer (2026).
  2. Assess the economic impact of implementing the FMP Protocol under explicit scenarios corresponding to the Protocol's three phases (right of entry; right of residence; right of establishment) and to variable-geometry coalitions of ratifying States, against a baseline that reflects existing unilateral and REC-level liberalisation, focusing on:
  1. Trade (including intra-African trade and services)
  2. Tourism flows, business travel and intra-African air passenger traffic
  3. Labour markets (employment, skills mobility, productivity)
  4. Investment and business mobility
  5. Public finances (visa and permit revenue foregone; tax and social contributions of mobile workers; public service costs)
  6. Informal and small-scale cross-border trade, with gender-disaggregated analysis
  7. Remittances and diaspora investment
  8. Implementation costs (civil registration and identity systems, border management, recognition of qualifications) and labour-market adjustment risks in destination countries
  1. Analyze the linkages between mobility and AfCFTA, including:
  1. Trade in services and movement of service providers (Mode 4 commitments in Member States' schedules under the AfCFTA Protocol on Trade in Services, and movement of key personnel under the Protocol on Investment)
  2. Labour mobility and regional value chains
  3. Economic integration and competitiveness
  1. Analyse the integration linkages between the FMP Protocol, the AfCFTA and the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM), in the broader context of the Agenda 2063 flagship projects supported under BIASHARA, including:
  1. Mapping the FMP Protocol's three phases against the mobility-dependent provisions of the AfCFTA (Mode 4 commitments under the Protocol on Trade in Services, movement of key personnel under the Protocol on Investment, and the operational needs of the Guided Trade Initiative) and identifying where the absence of mobility rights constrains AfCFTA implementation
  2. Including intra-African air passenger flows as an outcome variable in the quantitative analysis, using AFCAC/IATA data and the SAATM Continental Study route dataset (AUC and IATA, 2021), to estimate the interaction between visa openness (Africa Visa Openness Index) and air service liberalisation (SAATM Solemn Commitment and implementation status)
  3. A three-flagship status snapshot for each case-study country – AfCFTA (ratification, tariff and services schedules), SAATM (commitment, implementation, intra-African seat capacity) and FMP (signature/ratification, visa openness score, work-permit regime) – identifying sequencing complementarities and joint quick wins, consistent with the Africa Regional Integration Index, which already measures visa openness and intra-regional flight connections jointly (UNECA, AU and AfDB, 2019)
  4. A short set of joint advocacy messages for Ministers of Finance, Trade, Transport and Interior, delivered as an Integration Linkages Note (maximum 15 pages plus the snapshot matrix) and incorporated as a chapter of the final report and reflected in the policy briefs
  1. Undertake a comparative analysis of regional mobility regimes (e.g., ECOWAS, EAC, SADC), examining:
  1. Institutional and legal frameworks
  2. Implementation practices and governance models
  3. Economic outcomes, measured with quantified indicators (migrant stocks and flows, cross-border trade, tourism arrivals, remittances), including the reasons why the rights of residence and establishment have lagged the right of entry, the effects of the January 2025 withdrawal of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger from ECOWAS, and reversal episodes (re-introduced visa requirements, electronic travel authorisations, border closures)
  1. Conduct exploratory case studies of 4–6 countries selected against explicit criteria – ratifying States; unilateral first movers (e.g., Rwanda, Kenya, Ghana, Benin, The Gambia, Seychelles); pivotal non-signatories (e.g., South Africa, Nigeria, Egypt); and at least one North African and one lusophone Member State –, focusing on:
  1. Early implementation approaches
  2. Enabling policy and institutional conditions
  3. Emerging economic benefits and challenges
  1. Identify key enabling factors and constraints affecting the economic impact of free movement, including regulatory, institutional, and political economy dimensions.
  2. Engage key stakeholders (AU institutions, RECs, Member States, private sector, tourism actors, and academia) to validate findings and ensure policy relevance.
  3. Develop policy recommendations and strategic guidance to:
  1. Maximize economic benefits of the FMP Protocol
  2. Align mobility frameworks with AfCFTA objectives
  3. Support Member States in implementation efforts
  4. Prepare a country-by-country readiness assessment of signatory States that have not yet ratified (a 'pathway to 15 ratifications'), presented in a traffic-light format compatible with the AU scorecards on AfCFTA, SAATM and FMP implementation
  1. Produce high-quality analytical outputs, including a final report and policy briefs tailored to AU decision-making processes. Outputs shall include the datasets, model files and code in reproducible form, a technical annex documenting methods, data and assumptions, and executive summaries in English and French, with Arabic and Portuguese versions of the policy briefs.
  1. Proposed Methodology

The study will adopt a mixed-methods analytical approach, combining quantitative and qualitative techniques to generate robust, policy-relevant, and forward-looking insights. The quantitative component shall, at a minimum, comprise: (i) gravity-model estimates of the effect of visa and permit restrictions on bilateral trade, tourism and intra-African air passenger flows, using a visa-restrictions index derived from the Africa Visa Openness Index (AfDB and AUC, 2025); (ii) event studies of the liberalisation and reversal episodes already observed (e.g., Rwanda 2013, Seychelles, Kenya 2024, Ghana 2025, Benin 2025, the ECOWAS decision of 2024 to abolish the 90-day limit); (iii) a labour-mobility scenario model (computable general equilibrium or a calibrated partial-equilibrium model) reporting results by phase of the Protocol and by country of origin and destination, extending the benefit-cost approach of Maskus (2023) beyond skilled labour; and (iv) fiscal incidence analysis for the case-study countries following the approach of OECD and ILO (2018). Data sources shall include the Africa Visa Openness Index series, UN DESA international migrant stocks, the AU Report on Labour Migration Statistics in Africa (STATAFRIC), AFCAC/IATA air traffic data and the SAATM Continental Study dataset (AUC and IATA, 2021), UN Tourism arrivals, World Bank/KNOMAD remittance data, COMESA and EAC small-scale cross-border trade surveys, the Freemove Project regime dataset (Acosta and van der Baaren, 2024), and national statistics.

This will be complemented by qualitative research, including key informant interviews with AU institutions, RECs, Member State representatives, private sector actors, and technical experts. A comparative case study approach will be applied, focusing on a targeted sample of regional mobility regimes and selected first-mover countries (approximately 4–6 cases) to ensure analytical depth while maintaining geographic representation.

The analysis will be structured around a comparative framework examining institutional arrangements, policy environments, and observed mobility practices. Findings will be validated through stakeholder consultations to ensure accuracy, relevance, and alignment with policy needs.

This approach is designed to balance analytical rigor, depth, and feasibility within the assignment timeline, while avoiding overly broad or non-implementable coverage.

Phase 2: A Continental Study on Public Perceptions of Free Movement of Persons in Africa: Comparative Analysis of Regional and Continental Mobility Dynamics

The study will answer a central analytical question:

  • What factors explain differences in public and stakeholder perceptions of regional and continental mobility frameworks, including their perceived feasibility, benefits, risks and implications for free movement? ?

Understanding how and why perceptions of regional and continental mobility frameworks differ is important for advancing continental integration. These perceptions may be shaped by a range of economic, social, political and institutional factors, including concerns around employment and job competition, irregular migration, security, migration governance and national sovereignty. The study will examine how these factors influence both public attitudes and stakeholder positions on the ratification and implementation of the FMP Protocol.

Continental survey evidence shows majority public support (56 per cent) for free movement within regions, alongside a widespread perception that crossing borders to work or trade is difficult and divided views on the economic effects of immigration (Afrobarometer, 2026). Paradoxically, the hesitation documented to date is largely at State level – sovereignty, security, revenue and the institutional separation between trade and interior ministries (ECA and AUC, 2023). No survey has yet asked citizens about a continental protocol as distinct from their regional regime. The analysis shall therefore distinguish government and elite positions from public attitudes, and shall include a continental-versus-regional comparison by design.

In this context, the African Union Commission seeks to undertake a comprehensive study to assess public perceptions of mobility across Africa, identify key drivers of fear and resistance, and generate evidence-based policy recommendations. The study will inform policy design, advocacy strategies, and labour mobility frameworks aligned with AfCFTA implementation, thereby strengthening the AU’s capacity to advance regional integration, intra-African trade, and economic transformation.

  1. Objective of the Assignment

The overall objective of this consultancy is to:

  1. Assess public perceptions of mobility, migration, and labour movement across Africa, with particular focus on concerns related to security, employment, and migration governance.
  2. Analyze the comparative dynamics between regional and continental mobility frameworks, testing the hypothesis that regional mobility regimes are perceived as more feasible and manageable than continental initiatives, and distinguishing public attitudes from government and elite positions.
  3. Identify key socio-political, economic, and security-related drivers of fear, resistance, and acceptance influencing public attitudes toward free movement.
  4. Develop actionable, evidence-based recommendations to inform:
    1. Ratification and implementation of the Free Movement of Persons Protocol
    2. AU public communication and advocacy strategies
    3. Labour mobility frameworks aligned with AfCFTA implementation
  1. Scope of Work

The consultant will undertake the following tasks:

1. Literature and Policy Review: Conduct a structured review of existing literature, AU policy frameworks, REC protocols, and empirical studies on migration, mobility, and labour movement in Africa, including AfCFTA-related mobility dynamics. The review shall include political-economy analyses of African migration governance (Hirsch, 2021; Zanker, 2019; Bisong, 2022; Chime et al., 2023; Maunganidze, 2022) and the perception evidence in Afrobarometer (2026).

2. Mapping and Analysis of Public Perceptions: Map and analyze public perceptions across a selected sample of AU Member States and RECs focusing on:

  • Security concerns (e.g., terrorism, cross-border crime)
  • Employment and labour market competition
  • Migration governance and irregular migration

Data sources will include:

  • Existing datasets (Afrobarometer Round 10, 2024/25, and earlier rounds; national and regional perception surveys)
  • Key informant interviews (government, AU/REC officials, private sector, academia)
  • Focus group discussions and a survey experiment in 6–8 Member States testing framing effects (continental versus regional versus bilateral mobility; skilled versus less-skilled workers; reciprocity), with the sample, countries and instruments to be specified in the inception report against the budget envelope
  • Media and digital narrative analysis
  • Message testing of candidate advocacy narratives, to inform the strategic communication guidance
  • All primary data collection shall comply with research ethics approval, informed consent and applicable data protection requirements, to be set out in the inception report

3. Comparative Assessment of Regional Mobility Regimes: Using the same case set as Phase 1 (Task 4) to avoid duplication, undertake a comparative assessment of selected regional mobility regimes (e.g., ECOWAS, EAC, SADC), examining:

  • Levels of public acceptance and trust
  • Implementation practices and governance models
  • Perceived economic and social benefits and risks

4. Analysis of Divergence Between Regional and Continental Mobility Frameworks: Analyze the divergence between regional and continental mobility frameworks, focusing on:

  • Differences in public trust and political acceptance
  • Perceived risks versus benefits at the continental level
  • Structural, institutional, and narrative factors influencing resistance

This analysis will draw on comparative evidence and stakeholder insights to explain why regional mobility regimes are often perceived as more feasible than continental initiatives.

5. Analyze Public Perceptions of Labour Mobility and Economic Opportunity: Examine how labour mobility and its perceived linkages to economic opportunity are understood by different stakeholder groups, focusing on:

  • Perceptions of job competition versus job creation
  • Public attitudes toward movement of workers and service providers
  • Perceived benefits and risks of skills mobility
  • Trust in national and continental institutions to manage labour mobility

This analysis will focus on perceptions, narratives, and attitudes, rather than measuring actual economic outcomes, and will complement the economic implications study.

6. Identify key narratives, misinformation trends, and political economy dynamics shaping public perceptions of free movement.

7. Engage key stakeholders (AU institutions, RECs, Member States, private sector, civil society, and academia) to validate findings and ensure policy relevance.

8. Develop policy recommendations and provide strategic guidance to:

  1. Address public fears and misconceptions
  2. Strengthen AU communication and advocacy strategies
  3. Align mobility policies with AfCFTA labour market needs
  4. Support Member States in advancing ratification and implementation of the Free Movement of Persons Protocol

9. Produce high-quality analytical outputs, including a final report and policy briefs tailored to AU decision-making processes.

  1. Proposed Methodology

The study will adopt a mixed-methods approach combining quantitative and qualitative techniques to ensure robust and policy-relevant findings. It will draw on existing datasets (such as Afrobarometer and national perception surveys), complemented by primary data collection (a survey experiment, focus group discussions and elite interviews with parliamentarians, immigration and labour officials) in a targeted sample of 6–8 Member States across the five AU regions, including at least one North African Member State.

Qualitative methods will include key informant interviews with government officials, AU/REC representatives, private sector actors, civil society, and academia, as well as focus group discussions where feasible.

The study will also incorporate media and digital narrative analysis to capture prevailing public discourse, misinformation trends, and framing of mobility issues. A comparative analytical framework will be applied across selected regions and countries to identify patterns of perception, drivers of resistance or acceptance, and variations between regional and continental mobility narratives. Findings will be validated through stakeholder consultations to ensure accuracy, representativeness, and policy relevance.

  1. Schedule for Completion of Tasks

The assignment is expected to be completed within 30 weeks from the date of contract signature. The two phases will run as parallel workstreams under a single joint inception report; the milestones below are expressed as weeks from contract signature. A validation workshop with Member States, RECs, the AfCFTA Secretariat and AFCAC will be held between the interim and final reports (week 18).

  1. Consultant’s Qualifications, Experience Requirements and Team Composition

The assignment will be undertaken by a consulting firm or consortium (for example, an economics firm partnering with a survey research organisation) with demonstrated expertise in conducting research on migration, regional integration, economic analysis, free movement of persons, and public perception research. The firm should meet the following requirements:

A. Firm Qualifications and Experience

  • Proven track record (minimum 10 years) in conducting research on migration, mobility, labour movement, or regional integration in Africa

The National Planning Authority has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Uganda Strengthening Public Investment and Asset Management for Growth and Resilience Operation (PIMPlus) project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include undertaking a comprehensive, evidence-based study to identify and address the challenges contributing to the ineffective implementation of local content requirements in Uganda’s public procurement and project implementation. The study will assess the legal and regulatory framework, institutional coordination and enforcement mechanisms, procurement practices, and the capacity of Ugandan enterprises and the local workforce to participate in major public infrastructure projects. It will also quantify the economic costs of implementation gaps, benchmark Uganda’s performance against relevant international best practices, and develop prioritized, costed and actionable recommendations, including an implementation roadmap, financing strategy and proposals for follow-on technical assistance and capacity building.

SADC SECRETARIAT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                             Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:            SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:            INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANCY TO ASSESS AND IMPLEMENT TISSTAT FOR TRADE IN SERVICES DATA PERTAINING TO STATISTICAL DATA OF 2 MEMBER STATES IN SADC REGION. BW-SADC-563174-CS-INDV

 

 

REFERENCE NUMBER: SADC/5/2/478

 

DATE OF ISSUE: 17 November 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the SADC Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services to assess and implement TISSAT for Trade in service data pertaining to statistical data of 2 member states in SADC region in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title                 :  Individual Consultant to assess and implement TISSAT for Trade in service data pertaining to statistical data of 2 member states in SADC region (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  8 months

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this exercise is to capacitate two Member States in the region towards production of disaggregated trade in services (TIS) statistics to support regional integration priorities on trade policies.

 

  1. Specific objectives

 

The specific objective of this assignment is to undertake a comprehensive scoping and assessment exercise within the respective national statistical systems (NSSs) of 2 Member States and to implement TISSTAT tool for production and dissemination of detailed TIS statistics in one Member State.

 

  1. Expected results

 

The consultant is expected to achieve the following results in the following chronological order:

  • Scoping and Assessment Reports for 2 Member States (one for each) on statistical and institutional matters; and
  • Findings Report of TISSTAT in one Member State for collection of TIS statistics based on pilot exercise pertaining to statistical matters.

 

 

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by a consultant with in-depth knowledge in trade in services statistics and TISSTAT tool management.  The specific profile is provided below:

Qualifications and Skills

    • A minimum of a Degree in statistics, economics or related field. A Masters degree and above shall be an advantage.

 

General Professional Experience

    • The Consultant must have at least 15 years of specific experience in production and dissemination in economic statistics, in particular on external sector statistics such as Balance of Payments and TIS statistics.

 

Specific Professional Experience

    • Demonstrated experience of doing a scoping and assessment of countries for implementation of TISSTAT on statistics and institutional factors in at least 2 countries;

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-2.5-EUE-7-R1 – Senior Expert on Optimizing the Network of Vocational Training Institutions)

 

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

GPE TF0D0613

 

Assignment Title: Senior Expert on Optimizing the Network of Vocational Training Institutions

No. LEARN-2.5-EUE-7-R1

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of this assignment is to provide expert and analytical support to the MoES in coordinating activities for preparing regional plans for the formation of the network of vocational and professional pre-higher education institutions by local authorities, according to the Methodological Guidelines for Forming the Network of Institutions of Vocational and Professional Pre-higher Education, approved by the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine Order No. 216-r of March 4, 2026.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 Kyiv time December 04, 2026.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

Consulting Services (Individual Consultant)

Senior Expert on Optimizing the Network of Vocational Training Institutions

Contract No. LEARN-2.5-EUE-7-R1

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project

GPE TF0D0613

  1. Background

 

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln  provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675.9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln.

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, a Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) was signed between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (Loan No. K019-UA) in the amount of $286 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

II. OBJECTIVE OF THE TASK

The purpose of this assignment is to provide expert and analytical support to the MoES in coordinating activities for preparing regional plans for the formation of the network of vocational and professional pre-higher education institutions by local authorities, according to the Methodological Guidelines for Forming the Network of Institutions of Vocational and Professional Pre-higher Education, approved by the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine Order No. 216-r of March 4, 2026.

The expert will ensure that each region moves forward with the preparation of regional plans for formation of the network of vocational and professional pre-higher education institutions during the assignment period.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant will provide the following services, including but not limited to:

  • Coordinate engagement with regional teams and support the work of regional working groups;
  • Conduct consultations and working discussions with representatives of regional administrations, education departments, and other relevant stakeholders;
  • Provide guidance on the application of the Methodological Recommendations;
  • Deliver training on the use of analytical dashboards and tools for education network planning;
  • Provide advisory support to regional working groups responsible for developing regional plans for the establishment and optimization of vocational and professional pre-higher education networks, including guidance on the collection, analysis, and interpretation of data related to education networks, demographic trends, and labour market needs;
  • Develop and substantiate strategic recommendations for the optimization of education institution networks;
  • Monitor the progress of regional plan preparation and provide regular reports to the Project team.

IV. REPORTING

The Consultant will report to and cooperate with the Project Coordinator (Co-Coordinator) and work under the supervision of the General Director of the Directorate. For operational matters, the Consultant will coordinate his/her activities with the Head of the World Bank Operations Management Unit, ensuring effective interaction and support during project implementation.

The onsultant will prepare:

  • Monthly reports on services provided within the project execution;
  • Regular progress reports on the work with regions;
  • Analytical notes on the status of regional plans preparation.

V. RESOURCES PROVIDED

The MoES will provide the onsultant with the necessary information in a timely manner to carry out his/her duties. The MoES will also ensure the Consultant has a work station, including the necessary equipment to perform his/her functions (e.g., PC, communication tools, and office equipment).

VI. QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

L’INTITULE DE LA MISSION DE CONSULTANT : « Assistance technique en gestion des réserves, trésorerie et renforcement des capacités de la Banque de la République du Burundi (BRB) ».

N° DE REFERENCE (selon le Plan de Passation des marchés) : BI-ADB-571145-CS-INDV.

La République du Burundi a obtenu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet pour l’Emploi et la Transformation Economique (PRETE), et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Assistance technique en gestion des réserves, trésorerie et renforcement des capacités de la Banque de la République du Burundi (BRB) ».

Les services de consultants (« les services ») consistent à renforcer la capacité institutionnelle de la Banque de la République du Burundi (BRB) à gérer les réserves officielles conformément aux meilleures pratiques internationales à travers les objectifs spécifiques suivants : (i) établir et à affiner les structures de gouvernance et les cadres de politique de gestion des réserves, (ii) élaborer et mettre en œuvre une allocation stratégique d’actifs alignée sur les objectifs et les contraintes de la BRB, (iii) renforcer les pratiques de gestion du portefeuille et des risques, y compris la mesure et l'établissement de rapports sur les performances, (iv) élaborer un dispositif de reporting des risques et fournir un renforcement des capacités pratiques adapté aux besoins de la BRB, (v) améliorer les opérations de trésorerie et les accords avec les dépositaires, (vi) renforcer les capacités au niveau des fonctions support telles que les technologies de l'information, les services juridiques, et l'audit interne à travers de formations ciblées pour renforcer les compétences du personnel. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(Consultant Services – Individual Consultant)

Country: Republic of Kosovo
Project Name: Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening (KOMPAS)
Loan No.: IDA 75410
Assignment Title: Independent Technical QA Consultant – Architect
Reference No.: TBD
Issued on: 20 November 2026

Background

The Government of Kosovo has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening Project (KOMPAS), including its Additional Financing (AF) from the Pandemic Fund, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The primary objective of this assignment is to provide independent technical quality assurance and professional advice to the Ministry of Health (MoH or “the Client”) on architectural designs and project plans for health infrastructure investments financed under KOMPAS, including the targeted refurbishment of laboratory spaces and other relevant facilities supported by the Project. The Consultant will review relevant technical documentation, assess conformity with applicable requirements, observe relevant pre-construction activities, and provide findings and recommendations to support the Client's decision-making on the designs’ completeness, technical consistency, functionality and compliance with applicable requirements. The role is advisory and does not include responsibility for design preparation, design approval, construction supervision, or contract administration.

The Consultant will be engaged on an intermittent basis for six (6) months from contract signature, with an estimated maximum input of sixty (60) person-days. Inputs will be requested and agreed with the PCU based on the needs and timing of KOMPAS-financed design and pre-construction activities.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

The Ministry of Health now invites eligible individual consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested candidates should submit:

  • A Letter of Expression of Interest
  • A detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Copies of diplomas and relevant certifications
  • References for similar assignments (if available)

Selection Method

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultants (IC) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Qualifications and Experience Requirements

The Consultant shall meet the following minimum qualifications:

  • A valid professional license as an architect (Category [A/B]), issued by the Chamber of Architects of the Republic of Kosovo (OARK) under Law No. 08/L-012 on the Chambers of Architects and Engineers in the Field of Construction, or a license issued outside Kosovo and recognized by the Chamber;
  • Continued validity of the license, and membership in good standing of the Chamber, for the full duration of the contract.
  • Master's degree in Architecture, or equivalent, from an accredited institution.
  • At least ten (10) years of professional experience in architectural design, technical review of architectural drawings and specifications, and quality assurance of building projects;
  • At least three (3) assignments involving independent technical review of architectural designs;
  • Experience in the design or technical review of at least three (3) healthcare facility projects (e.g., hospitals, primary healthcare centers);
  • Experience in the design or technical review of healthcare waste management and/or laboratory facilities is desirable.
  • Proficiency in CAD and architectural design software (e.g., AutoCAD, ArchiCAD, Revit or equivalent);
  • Thorough knowledge of Kosovo construction legislation, building regulations and technical standards;
  • Knowledge of international standards and guidelines for healthcare facility design is desirable;
  • Knowledge of applicable environmental, health and safety requirements relevant to healthcare infrastructure is desirable.
  • Fluency in Albanian and English, written and spoken;
  • Working knowledge of Serbian is desirable.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 16:00.

Expressions of Interest must be delivered electronically (by e-mail) to the address below no later than 04 December 2026 at 16:00 local time. Expressions of Interest received after the deadline will not be considered.

Ministry of Health

World Bank Loan/Credit Name: Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening- KOMPAS

Assignment name:  Independent Technical QA Consultant – Architect

 

  1. Background

Referring to the Financing Agreement between the Republic of Kosovo and the International Development Association for the Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening Project (KOMPAS), the KOMPAS Project (P179831) was approved on 07 May, 2024. The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to strengthen institutional capacity and governance for quality of care in the Kosovo health system.

The following are the components of the project:

Component 1: Strengthening key health system building blocks for Quality of Care (QoC)

The objective of this component is to support aspects of public health/Pandemic Preparedness and Response (PPR), service delivery, and health financing (strategic purchasing), that will help unblock the bottlenecks in the structural and process of care. This component will include three sub-components, outlined below:

Subcomponent 1.1 Improving service delivery. This subcomponent is aligned with the strategic objectives of the forthcoming Health Sector Strategy for 2023-2030 and builds on the recommendations of the recent World Bank’s report highlighting the quality aspect of noncommunicable diseases (NCD) management in Kosovo.

Subcomponent 1.2: Developing and implementing strategic purchasing for quality. This subcomponent will support the development and implementation of key strategic purchasing elements which are not in place in Kosovo but are critical for both structural and process aspects of quality care.

Subcomponent 1.3 Strengthening public health and PPR. This subcomponent will build on activities carried out under the Kosovo Emergency COVID-19 Response Project (P173819) in the areas of PPR. It will support key areas of the Action Plan of the National Program on Communicable Diseases (2022) and the Action Plan for HCWM (2023).

Additional Financing (AF) resources support: (i) scaling up AMR surveillance and analytics; (ii) procurement of laboratory equipment and consumables based on national capacity assessments; (iii) strengthening biosafety and biosecurity through risk assessments, equipment, and standard operating procedures; and (iv) targeted refurbishment of laboratory spaces to improve workflows and accreditation readiness. The AF also funds expansion of HCWM infrastructure and practices, including equipment and operational systems, alongside workforce training for laboratory staff, frontline health workers, and epidemiological surge capacity (including training, simulation exercises, and emergency response preparedness)

Component 2: Developing an Integrated Health Information System (IHIS): The objective of this component is to support the design, development, and implementation of an integrated digital health ecosystem that is critical for the functioning of the entire health system. The foundational and key strategic IHIS building blocks will set the digitized health data environment to support health service delivery and decision-making.

This component will include three sub-components, outlined below:

Subcomponent 2.1: Establishing foundational building blocks of IHIS. This subcomponent will support the establishment of critical elements of foundational environment (Enterprise Architecture) for digital health systems implementation, including: (i) the legal and regulatory framework for transformed health services delivery through digital systems utilization; (ii) the assessment and design of Master Data Management standards and systems, such as foundational registries and common coding and classification systems; (iii) design and implementation of the Health Information Exchange services; and (iv) upgrade of hardware platforms on central locations and in health facilities.

Subcomponent 2.2: Digital health support for improvement in QoC. Implementation of Component 1 will require finalization of the implementation and upgrade of the basic health information system (BHIS). Currently, the BHIS is not fully implemented in all Primary Health Care (PHC) facilities and with full functionality. This subcomponent will support: (i) rolling out the BHIS to all PHC facilities (including finalization of patient empanelment and zoning); (ii) upgrading the BHIS functions (automatic update of codes from key registries and allowing dashboard and smart reporting on facility level); and (iii) upgrading the integration with e-Referrals system and introduction of e-Appointments.

Subcomponent 2.3: Implementation of IHIS strategic systems. The eHealth Feasibility Study envisages full digitalization of the health sector in Kosovo to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of service delivery, clinical decision support, health financing, pandemic preparedness and public health functions, supply chain for pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals, health workforce management, and health system management and policy making.

AF financing under Component 2 strengthens and operationalizes digital foundations critical for real-time surveillance and data-driven response. The AF supports development and rollout of an integrated LIMS, enhanced disease surveillance and early warning systems, and improved interoperability between surveillance platforms, laboratory systems, and analytics tools under a One Health approach. Resources finance software development and adaptation, targeted IT hardware, and technical assistance to ensure alignment with the modular and interoperable IHIS architecture defined under KOMPAS. By embedding these systems within the broader health information exchange ecosystem, the AF enables timely data sharing, performance monitoring, and cross-border information exchange, amplifying the preparedness impact of ongoing digital health investments.

Component 3: Project Management, Monitoring, and Evaluation: The objective of this component is to support overall project administration, including project management, fiduciary functions (procurement, financial management (FM)), monitoring and evaluation, environmental and social compliance, and regular monitoring of and reporting on project implementation. The component will finance consulting services, including consultants to staff the Project Coordination Unit (PCU), as well as office equipment, training, audits, filing systems, and operating costs. 

Under Component 3, the AF provides additional resources to support effective implementation, coordination, and oversight of the expanded scope of activities. This includes financing for incremental PCU staffing and specialist support (including procurement, fiduciary, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), and environmental and social standards-related functions), operating costs associated with the AF scale-up, and strengthened M&E capacity. AF resources ensure that implementation of PF-financed activities is fully integrated into existing project management, reporting, and results monitoring systems, thereby maintaining fiduciary integrity, implementation speed, and accountability

  1. Objective of the Assignment

The primary objective of this assignment is to provide independent technical quality assurance and professional advice to the Ministry of Health (MoH or “the Client”) on architectural designs and project plans for health infrastructure investments financed under KOMPAS, including the targeted refurbishment of laboratory spaces and other relevant facilities supported by the Project. The Consultant will review relevant technical documentation, assess conformity with applicable requirements, observe relevant pre-construction activities, and provide findings and recommendations to support the Client's decision-making on the designs’ completeness, technical consistency, functionality and compliance with applicable requirements. The role is advisory and does not include responsibility for design preparation, design approval, construction supervision, or contract administration.

  1. Scope of Work

The Independent Technical QA Consultant – Architect (hereinafter “the Consultant”) shall provide independent professional review and technical advice to the Client on architectural designs and project plans for health infrastructure investments financed under the KOMPAS Project, including its Additional Financing (AF) from the Pandemic Fund, namely: (i) targeted refurbishment of laboratory spaces to improve workflows, biosafety and biosecurity, and accreditation readiness; (ii) expansion of healthcare waste management (HCWM) infrastructure; and (iii) other rehabilitation or adaptation works in health facilities financed under the Project, as applicable.

In this capacity, the Consultant shall perform the following functions:

3.1 Architectural/design quality assurance

  • Review the design brief and existing-condition surveys for each facility (measured, structural, building services, and hazardous materials such as asbestos), and advise whether user requirements have been agreed with facility management and clinical and laboratory staff.
  • Conduct independent reviews of architectural designs and related documentation at the concept, preliminary and detailed design stages, within turnaround times agreed with the PCU, covering completeness, technical consistency, coordination with engineering designs and medical/laboratory equipment, and constructability.
  • Record comments in a design review log, flag matters requiring specialist review, and advise the Client whether revised submissions address the comments transmitted by the Client to the designers.
  • Propose value engineering options for the Client’s consideration, where relevant.

3.2 Compliance with applicable building/technical requirements

  • Assess compliance of the designs with the design brief, approved standards, Kosovo building codes and technical regulations, including structural, fire and life safety, universal access, climate resilience and energy efficiency requirements.
  • Cross-check drawings, specifications and bills of quantities for consistency, re-measure a sample of high-value and high-risk items, and review cost estimates against current market prices in Kosovo to flag budget risks.
  • Check that technical specifications are performance-based and that any brand names are followed by “or equivalent.”

3.3 Healthcare/laboratory functionality and safety considerations

  • Review the functionality of layouts and of patient, staff, specimen, material and waste flows, including infection prevention and control (IPC) requirements.
  • For laboratory spaces, review whether the architectural design adequately addresses biosafety and biosecurity requirements, workflow efficiency and accreditation readiness, taking into account the national laboratory capacity and biosafety/biosecurity risk assessments, where available.
  • For HCWM infrastructure, review whether the designs provide for the safe segregation, storage, handling and treatment of healthcare waste, in line with applicable regulations and the Action Plan for HCWM.
  • Review design documentation for conformity with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework as reflected in the ESCP, ESMF and site-specific instruments of KOMPAS and the AF, as applicable, and coordinate with the PCU Environmental and Social Specialist on how the designs and specifications address hazardous materials (including asbestos), construction and demolition waste, and health and safety requirements for works in operational health facilities.

3.4 Pre-construction site observations

  • Carry out site visits early in the design stage, before bidding and during pre-construction, to check that designs reflect actual site conditions and to observe preparatory activities, and recommend further clarifications or investigations where needed.
  • When requested by the Client, advise on proposed design changes with architectural implications arising before the start of works, including their technical justification and impact on cost and time.

3.5 Reporting and technical coordination

  • Prepare written technical review reports summarizing identified issues, observations and recommendations for consideration by the Client and the responsible design consultant.
  • Before each bidding process, prepare a Readiness Review Report summarizing outstanding issues and risks, to inform the Client’s decision on whether to proceed with bidding.
  • When requested, assist the Client in preparing responses to bidders’ clarification requests on architectural and technical matters, and any resulting addenda.
  • Participate in coordination meetings and design workshops when requested by the PCU.
  • Communicate findings only to the Client; the Consultant shall not review or respond to submissions on behalf of the design and supervision consultant or the Engineer.

The Consultant shall have no authority to approve, reject or certify designs, issue instructions to designers, contractors or other parties, or commit the Client to any change in scope, cost or schedule.

The Consultant’s review and technical review reports shall not constitute design approval, certification, or acceptance, nor relieve the designers of their professional responsibility for the designs, including their compliance with applicable codes, regulations, standards, and contractual requirements.

The Consultant shall not assume the responsibilities of the design and supervision consultant, Engineer, Contractor, or any other party contractually responsible for the design or implementation of the works.

  1. Deliverables

The Consultant will provide, as requested through individual assignments agreed with the PCU, the following deliverables:

  • Technical review notes/reports for architectural designs and related documentation reviewed under the assignment;
  • Site visit notes summarizing relevant observations and recommended follow-up actions;
  • Written technical comments on revised documentation, including whether previously identified issues have been addressed;
  • Readiness Review Reports prior to each bidding process, as described in Section 3.5;
  • Monthly activity reports and timesheets, summarizing tasks undertaken, findings and recommendations, and person-days utilized; and
  • Final assignment report, summarizing work undertaken, major technical issues identified, recommendations provided, lessons learned and outstanding matters, if any.

All deliverables shall be prepared in English and submitted in electronic format to the PCU Project Coordinator, as the designated PCU representative, for review and acceptance. The Project Coordinator will confirm acceptance or request revisions within ten (10) working days of receipt, in consultation with the relevant MoH department(s) on technical matters, as needed.

  1. Reporting and Institutional Arrangements

The Consultant shall report to the Project Coordinator of the KOMPAS Project Coordination Unit (PCU) at the Ministry of Health, who will be responsible for agreeing individual assignments, reviewing and accepting deliverables, and approving monthly timesheets.

Monthly activity reports and timesheets approved by the Project Coordinator shall constitute the basis for payment. The PCU will share the Consultant’s key findings and recommendations with the Secretary General of the Ministry of Health, as necessary.

The Consultant shall coordinate, as necessary, with the relevant departments of the Ministry of Health and the design and supervision consultant to obtain information and clarifications required for the performance of the assignment.

The Consultant will be based at the Ministry of Health in Pristina and will undertake site visits to relevant project locations as required.

  1. Qualifications and Experience Requirements

The successful candidate should possess the following qualifications:

Professional License

  • A valid professional license as an architect (Category [A/B]), issued by the Chamber of Architects of the Republic of Kosovo (OARK) under Law No. 08/L-012 on the Chambers of Architects and Engineers in the Field of Construction, or a license issued outside Kosovo and recognized by the Chamber;
  • Continued validity of the license, and membership in good standing of the Chamber, for the full duration of the contract.

Education

  • Master's degree in Architecture, or equivalent, from an accredited institution.

Professional Experience

  • At least ten (10) years of professional experience in architectural design, technical review of architectural drawings and specifications, and quality assurance of building projects;
  • At least three (3) assignments involving independent technical review of architectural designs;
  • Experience in the design or technical review of at least three (3) healthcare facility projects (e.g., hospitals, primary healthcare centers);
  • Experience in the design or technical review of healthcare waste management and/or laboratory facilities is desirable.

Technical Competencies

  • Proficiency in CAD and architectural design software (e.g., AutoCAD, ArchiCAD, Revit or equivalent);
  • Thorough knowledge of Kosovo construction legislation, building regulations and technical standards;
  • Knowledge of international standards and guidelines for healthcare facility design is desirable;
  • Knowledge of applicable environmental, health and safety requirements relevant to healthcare infrastructure is desirable.

Languages

  • Fluency in Albanian and English, written and spoken;
  • Working knowledge of Serbian is desirable.
  1. Duration and Payment

The Consultant will be engaged on an intermittent basis for six (6) months from contract signature, with an estimated maximum input of sixty (60) person-days. Inputs will be requested and agreed with the PCU based on the needs and timing of KOMPAS-financed design and pre-construction activities.

The Consultant shall be remunerated on a time-based basis at the agreed daily rate. Payments will be made monthly for the actual person-days approved, supported by timesheets approved by the PCU Project Coordinator and the corresponding outputs produced and accepted during the reporting period, in accordance with Section 4.

The contract shall use the World Bank Standard Time-Based Contract, with all terms and conditions specified therein.

  1. Client Contribution

The Consultant will be based and work at the MoH premises in Pristina. The MoH will provide reasonable access to relevant project documentation and information required for the performance of the assignment and will facilitate coordination with relevant institutions, project staff, and other stakeholders as necessary.

  1. Selection Process

Experienced and qualified individuals will be selected in accordance with the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers ("the Regulations"), September 2023, based on an open call for Individual Consultants (IC) Selection.

The consultant will be selected based on:

  • The overall consultant qualification (50%);
  • Relevant work experience (50%).

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

 

Country: Lebanon

Project Name: GFPP for Lebanon Digital Acceleration Project (LDAP)

GFPP Grant No.: TF0C8895

Project No.: P181954

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Development of a Government Cloud Policy Framework for Lebanon

Reference No.: LB-OMSAR-537761-CS-INDV

The Republic of Lebanon represented by the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform (OMSAR) has received a Grant (# TF0C8895) from the World Bank’s Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this grant for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include establishing the foundations of Lebanon's government cloud policy framework through three connected outputs: (i) a Statement of Policy Principles, grounded in international good practice and validated with Lebanese stakeholders; (ii) a draft Government Cloud Policy, prepared as a binding policy instrument in a form suitable for formal adoption; and (iii) a Cloud Policy Framework Architecture and Institutional Responsibility Matrix that position the Policy within the wider framework, assign ownership of each element, and identify the follow-on workstreams required to complete it.. The assignment is expected to be completed in approximately 14 weeks from the Contract’s Commencement Date.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest – Annex I.

The Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform (OMSAR) now invites eligible individual consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide:

  1. A curriculum vitae (CV) demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience, and
  2. A brief Methodology and Work Plan (not exceeding 5 pages) outlining the proposed technical approach and logical sequencing of activities to fulfil the scope of work.

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

The Consultant must meet the following minimum requirements:

  • An advanced degree in public policy, law, ICT, digital government, information systems, or a related field;
  • At least ten (10) years of professional experience in digital government, digital transformation, ICT policy, or cloud strategy and governance;
  • Demonstrated experience drafting government cloud policies or comparable binding digital-government policy instruments (e.g., policies, directives, decrees, or regulations) that were subsequently adopted by a government or public institution;
  • Demonstrated comparative knowledge of government digital policy frameworks across multiple jurisdictions, including their approaches to relevant areas such as data classification, security standards, provider assurance, and enforcement.
  • Good familiarity with public financial management, public budgeting, and public procurement, preferably in Lebanon;
  • Experience working in developing countries and/or fragile and conflict-affected contexts is desirable; experience in the Middle East and North Africa region is an advantage;
  • Oral and written proficiency and ability to draft policy instruments in either English or Arabic; knowledge of both languages is an advantage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (September 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (09:00 AM to 04:00 PM Beirut Time).

Expressions of interest (including CV and a methodology/work plan not exceeding 5 pages) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by COB December 4, 2026.
