for consulting services for the preparation, organisation and administration of the field trial of the International Computer and Information Literacy Study (ICILS)

 

Contract No. LEARN-2.1-ICILS-1

World Bank Project ID No.: P504171, Grant Number: TF0C5794

 

I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine and the World Bank have signed the agreements for the Program "Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program" (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN). The objectives of the LEARN are: to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system.

The total financing for the Operation is US$451 million using a combination of the World Bank's financial instruments: Program-for-Results (PforR) complemented by Investment Project Financing (IPF).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is funded by a US$235 million credit provided by Bank resources, supported by credit enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT NUMBER 7626-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN NUMBER 9721-UA). Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT NUMBER 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0C5794).

Furthermore, US$31.1 million in Additional Financing is provided through grant resources, consisting of US$30.0 million from the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund and US$1.1 million from the Global Partnership for Education Fund. This additional financing is formalized under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0D0612; GPE GRANT NUMBER TF0D0613), and supports activities related to the continued implementation of the Program.

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science's (MoES) Strategic Action Plan.

The Operation will focus on supporting the Strategic Action Plan Priority 2: School education and the New Ukrainian School (NUS). The continuation of the NUS reform is a key priority of the MoES.

The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

For this program, "teaching and learning conditions" refer to three critical factors of education service delivery:

  • safety, including shelters as a pre-condition for schools to open for in-person learning and free and inclusive school bus transportation for students living further distances from schools;
  • learning materials, especially updated textbooks and age-appropriate learning materials in line with the NUS model; and
  • teachers trained on NUS standards, principles, and the use of the updated learning materials.

Meanwhile, "management capacity of the education system" refers to institutional capabilities to plan, allocate, and monitor resources based on robust data at the student and school levels.

The NUS Implementation Office (NIO) was established by the Ministry as an advisory and consultative body. The NIO's primary purpose is to support and implement the New Ukrainian School (NUS) reform by providing expert guidance, strategic oversight, and coordination of reform initiatives across Ukraine.

 

II. GENERAL INFORMATION

The Consultant's Assignment is to provide professional consulting services for the preparation, organisation and administration of the field trial of the International Computer and Information Literacy Study (ICILS) in Ukraine in 2027, with the support of the study organiser, the International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement (IEA). The Assignment is implemented as part of the Assessments component of the World Bank-financed project 'Improving Access to and Resilience of Education in Times of Crisis in Ukraine' (LEARN). Implementation is coordinated by the New Ukrainian School Implementation Office (NIO), which ensures the alignment of the Assignment with the New Ukrainian School (NUS) Roadmap and consolidated reporting on ICILS as part of LEARN programme support.

The purpose of the field trial is to pilot the national study instruments, methodological, organisational and technical procedures, sampling mechanisms, school recruitment, assessment and questionnaire administration, quality control, scoring and coding of responses, as well as data processing and transmission. The field trial results are intended to identify and address potential content-related, organisational and technical issues and confirm Ukraine's readiness to conduct the ICILS main survey in 2028.

The field trial is expected to cover approximately 25 general secondary education institutions, 750 students and 375 teachers.

Ukraine's participation in ICILS 2028 forms part of the implementation of its commitments in the context of European integration in education. The National Programme for the Adaptation of Ukrainian Legislation to European Union Law (EU acquis), approved by Resolution No. 438 of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine dated 1 April 2026, includes Task 5 under Objective 4 of Chapter 26 “Education and Science” of Cluster 3: “Ensuring Ukraine's participation in international studies assessing the level of digital skills of learners and teaching staff.”

The EU Digital Education Action Plan through 2027 includes an action to improve monitoring and support cross-country collection of data on students' digital skills through participation in ICILS, in order to better understand existing gaps and strengthen the evidence base for measures aimed at addressing them, as well as establishment of an EU-level target for students' digital competence: by 2030, reduce to below 15% the share of 13–14-year-old students who underachieve in computer and information literacy. The Council Resolution on a strategic framework for European cooperation in education and training towards the European Education Area and beyond (2021–2030) (2021/C 66/01) of 26 February 2021 and the Council Resolution on the second cycle of the strategic framework for European cooperation in education and training towards the European Education Area (2026–2030) (C/2026/3720) of 10 July 2026 establish the target of reducing, by 2030, the share of eighth-grade students with low achievement in computer and information literacy to below 15%. This indicator is calculated exclusively on the basis of ICILS results.

Ukraine's participation in ICILS is also driven by the implementation of national education policy. Pursuant to Article 12 of the Law of Ukraine “On Education”, development of the key competences including information and communication competence is one of the objectives of general secondary education. The Concept for the Implementation of State Policy in the Reform of General Secondary Education “New Ukrainian School” for the period until 2029, approved by Order No. 988-r of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine dated 14 December 2016, also identifies information and communication competence as one of the key competences of learners. In 2028, the study participants will be students studying under the new State Standard for Basic Secondary Education developed as part of this policy, which will make it possible, for the first time, to conduct an international assessment of the outcomes of the New Ukrainian School reform with respect to the development of students' information and communication competence. Participation in ICILS is embedded in the NUS Roadmap as the instrument for the international measurement of students' information and communication competence. ICILS 2028 will provide the first internationally comparable evidence on a learning outcome of the New Ukrainian School reform, as the 2028 cohort will have completed the full cycle of basic secondary education under the new State Standard.

Ukraine's participation in ICILS 2028 will provide objective and internationally comparable data on students' levels of computer and information literacy and computational thinking skills, as well as on educational, social, institutional and technological factors affecting their development. The study will also provide information on the use and integration of modern digital technologies, including artificial intelligence technologies, in the general secondary education system.

The results acquired after the main survey phase will establish baseline data for further monitoring of students' digital competences and contribute to improving education policy, state education standards, curricula and approaches to the organisation of the educational process. They will feed into the monitoring framework of the NUS Roadmap and will provide inputs for the national assessment system currently being developed by the Ukrainian Center for Educational Quality Assessment (UCEQA), in particular as regards the design of digital-competence assessment instruments, scaling procedures, and the use of context data in national monitoring. Consolidated findings will be reported by the NIO as part of LEARN programme reporting.

The results will also strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to collect, analyse and use data for the development and evaluation of evidence-based public policy in school education and the digital transformation of education.

Participation in the study will contribute to Ukraine's integration into the European Education Area, strengthen its participation in the international professional dialogue on education quality, and ensure the alignment and complementarity of ICILS with other international comparative studies of education quality in which Ukraine participates.

III. OBJECTIVES

The specific objectives of this Assignment are to:

  1. Ensure the preparation of the national school sampling frame in accordance with the international requirements of ICILS 2028, including defining coverage, exclusions and stratification variables, and support the sampling process carried out by the IEA International Study Center.
  2. Ensure the recruitment of educational institutions for participation in the field trial, organise interaction with the selected institutions, designate School Coordinators, and prepare samples of classes, and teachers, students lists at school level using the Online Survey Expert platform.
  3. Prepare national versions of the computer and information literacy and computational thinking assessment instruments through translation, linguistic adaptation and layout verification.
  4. Prepare national versions of the context questionnaires for students, teachers, school principals and digital technologies coordinators through translation, linguistic and structural adaptation, and layout verification.
  5. Ensure methodological and staffing readiness for data collection, including preparation of national manuals and methodological materials, participation in training and coordination activities organised by the IEA International Study Center, and training of School Coordinators, Test Administrators, technical support specialists, national quality assurance monitors (NQAMs), scorers and coders.
  6. Ensure the technical readiness of educational institutions, including checking the compatibility of computer equipment with ICILS 2028 software, testing access to the assessment instruments, identifying and resolving technical issues, organising technical support, and preparing backup computer equipment.
  7. Organise and conduct field-trial data collection in the sampled educational institutions in compliance with international procedures and quality requirements and within the timeframe aligned with the field trial schedule established by the IEA International Study Center.
  8. Ensure independent monitoring of study quality by engaging national quality assurance monitors, in a number consistent with the standards established by the IEA International Study Center, to observe assessment sessions, interview School Coordinators and Test Administrators, and consolidate monitoring results.
  9. Ensure the completeness and quality of field-trial data, including entering information on student and teacher participation, scoring responses to open-ended items, coding information on parents' or guardians' occupations, and checking the accuracy and consistency of scoring and coding.
  10. Ensure timely transmission to the IEA International Study Center of the complete set of data and documentation, completion of reporting forms required under international procedures, and interaction with the IEA International Study Center during data verification and processing.
  11. Establish the organisational, methodological and technical prerequisites for conducting the ICILS 2028 main survey, including further improvement of national instruments, procedures, manuals and methodological materials, quality control mechanisms and technical arrangements.
  12. Ensure the alignment of national ICILS implementation with the NUS Roadmap, including agreement of the implementation schedule, milestones and reporting points with the NIO as the unit coordinating the Assessments component of the LEARN project.

 

IV. SCOPE OF SERVICES

Under this Assignment, the Consultant shall provide the full cycle of preparation, organisation and implementation of the ICILS 2028 field trial in Ukraine, from preparing the national sampling frame and recruiting educational institutions to completion of data collection, scoring and coding, preparation of reporting documentation, and transmission of materials to the IEA International Study Center.

The field trial is expected to involve approximately 25 general secondary education institutions selected in accordance with IEA procedures. The field trial will include assessments of students' computer and information literacy and computational thinking, as well as context questionnaires for students, teachers, school principals and digital technologies coordinators.

The Consultant shall provide technical, organisational, methodological, linguistic and analytical support at all stages of the Assignment, as well as appropriate coordination with the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) (hereinafter - the Client), the New Ukrainian School Implementation Office (NIO), the IEA International Study Center, the Institute of Educational Analytics, the Ukrainian Center for Educational Quality Assessment (UCEQA), the State Service of Education Quality of Ukraine (SSEQU), educational institutions, and other involved institutions and specialists.

The Client shall serve as the primary point of contact for the Consultant and the lead institution responsible for national-level coordination. The Consultant shall coordinate day-to-day activities through the Client-designated focal point, in close cooperation with the NIO.

Matters requiring inter-agency agreement or decisions beyond the Consultant's authority shall be escalated to the Client-designated focal point, who shall coordinate their resolution with the NIO and other relevant institutions, as appropriate.

The Institute of Educational Analytics, the Ukrainian Center for Educational Quality Assessment, the State Service of Education Quality of Ukraine and other relevant institutions and specialists shall be involved as necessary, within their respective mandates and in accordance with relevant orders of the MoES.

 

All work shall be performed in accordance with the ICILS 2028 methodology, standard operating procedures, instructions, technical specifications and timelines established by the IEA International Study Center and agreed with the Client. The Consultant shall use the electronic platforms and information systems provided for the study, including IEA ICILS 2028 SharePoint, Online Survey Expert, StudyExpert and the ICILS Dashboard.

When performing the Assignment, the Consultant shall ensure:

  • confidentiality and appropriate protection of information and personal data of study participants;
  • secure storage of encryption keys, credentials and the linkage between national and randomised identifiers of general secondary education institutions;
  • compliance with quality and international comparability requirements, and documentation of all adaptations, deviations and non-standard situations;
  • readiness to respond to air-raid alerts, evacuations, power or communication outages, and other emergency circumstances;
  • timely reporting to the Client and the IEA International Study Center on the progress of work, identified risks and problems, and measures taken to address them;
  • proper documentation of work performed and preparation of the reporting and supporting materials required under the Assignment.

 

INCEPTION PHASE:

Purpose of the component.

At the beginning of the Assignment, an inception phase shall be conducted to confirm the implementation approach, the experts' readiness to commence work, the work plan and schedule, timelines, and quality assurance measures in accordance with the established scope of services. The inception phase shall commence on the effective date of the Contract and shall not exceed one (1) month.

The output of the inception phase shall be the submission to the Client for review and approval of an Inception Report, including:

  • an implementation plan for the ICILS 2028 national field trial, agreed with the IEA International Study Center;
  • the operational structure of the National Study Center with a clear allocation of functions, including the National Research Coordinator, National Data Manager, etc.;
  • coordination and communication mechanisms between the Client, the NIO as the unit coordinating the Assessments component of the LEARN project, the Consultant, the IEA International Study Center, educational institutions and other parties.

 

Social aspects, ethical conduct and prevention of SEA/SH (sexual exploitation and abuse / sexual harassment):

During the inception phase, before commencing work or engaging with stakeholders, all experts involved in the Assignment shall:

  • complete mandatory training and awareness-raising activities on the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse and sexual harassment (SEA/SH) in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) requirements;

  • familiarise themselves with the Emergency Preparedness and Response Manual.

 

Non-disclosure of confidential information

During the inception phase, prior to commencing work and obtaining access to confidential IEA materials, all experts involved in the Assignment shall:

  • sign and comply with the Confidentiality Agreement governing the use of the IEA ICILS 2028 SharePoint site.

 

Personal data protection

During the inception phase, prior to commencing work, the National Research Coordinator shall:

 

  • enter into a Joint Controller Agreement with the “Stichting I.E.A. Secretariaat Nederland” regarding joint control of personal data and subsequently provide reasonable assistance and conclude all necessary agreements to comply with IEA international data protection standards.

 

Component 1. Work on the school sample

Purpose of the component

This component is aimed at preparing the materials required for the IEA International Study Center to draw a representative sample of general secondary education institutions.

 

Scope of work

Under this component, the Consultant shall perform the following tasks.

    1. Analytical and conceptual preparation

The Consultant shall:

  • Conduct joint consultations with the Client, the IEA International Study Center, the Institute of Educational Analytics and the Ukrainian Center for Educational Quality Assessment, the State Service of Education Quality of Ukraine, agree on the parameters to be applied in preparing the sampling frame, namely coverage, exclusions and stratification variables, and obtain the information required to complete the sampling forms. The agreed parameters shall include, subject to agreement with the IEA International Study Center, indicators enabling subsequent disaggregation of results by characteristics relevant to NUS reform monitoring (inter alia participation in NUS pilot activities and receipt of digital equipment under LEARN), retained either as stratification variables or as analytical variables in the national sampling frame.
  • Prepare and ensure submission of the IEA International Study Center sampling forms via the IEA ICILS 2028 SharePoint site.
    1. Preparation of the sampling frame

The Consultant shall:

  • In coordination with the Institute of Educational Analytics, prepare the national sampling frame covering all general secondary education institutions that meet the criteria specified in the sampling forms, including randomised identifiers, indicators, stratification variables and exclusion codes, where applicable.
  • Ensure submission of an anonymised version of the national sampling frame containing randomised identifiers of general secondary education institutions via the IEA ICILS 2028 SharePoint site.
    1. Coordination of the sampling process

The Consultant shall:

  • Promptly inform the IEA International Study Center that the prepared sampling frame of general secondary education institutions has been submitted for the study.
  • Support the review of the sampling frame by the IEA International Study Center and respond to requests and clarifications.
  • Store the linkage between national and randomised identifiers securely and separately from the data transmitted to the IEA International Study Center.
  • Verify that the educational institutions selected for the field trial meet the eligibility criteria and have the operational capacity to participate.

 

Component 2. Recruitment of educational institutions and school-level sampling

Purpose of the component

This component is aimed at ensuring the participation in the field trial of the required number of educational institutions determined by the sample drawn by the IEA International Study Center, as well as work with the Online Survey Expert (OSE) platform and the selection of classes and teachers for study participation at school level using OSE.

Scope of work

Under this component, the Consultant shall perform the following tasks.

2.1. Recruitment of educational institutions for participation in the field trial

The Consultant shall:

  • In coordination with the Client and the NIO and other institutions as designated by the Client, including UCEQA, SSEQU, etc., prepare a communication strategy for recruiting educational institutions to participate in the field trial and supporting materials, including draft letters, information materials, texts for publication on social media, rules for interaction with educational institutions, etc. The communication strategy shall be consistent with the communication line of the New Ukrainian School reform and shall present ICILS as an element of NUS reform monitoring. Communication materials shall be agreed with the Client and the NIO and shall comply with the visual identity and disclaimer requirements of the LEARN project.
  • Communicate with educational institutions included in the sample and obtain their consent to participate in the study; where an institution declines, recruit the corresponding replacement institution identified in the sample (the indicative number of educational institutions participating in the field trial is 25).
  • Ensure that School Coordinators are designated in the educational institutions that confirm participation in the study, including communication with the institutions on the need to designate contact persons for further coordination of their participation.

 

2.2. School-level sampling using the Online Survey Expert (OSE) platform

The Consultant shall:

  • Participate in a webinar delivered by the IEA International Study Center on the use of the Online Survey Expert (OSE) platform.
  • Agree with the Client and other institutions as designated by the Client, on the procedure for submitting information to the platform, including persons responsible for providing such information and the rules for collecting and processing study participants' personal data.
  • Organise system access for authorised persons, securely store the encryption key and manage user accounts.
  • Ensure that information on the status of interaction with selected educational institutions and confirmation of their consent to participate in the field trial is entered into the system.
  • Ensure the collection and entry into OSE of lists of all target classes in the selected educational institutions and sampling parameters, and carry out class selection for participation in the study using OSE.
  • Ensure the preparation of lists of teachers teaching the target class and select teachers for participation in the study using OSE.
  • Ensure the preparation of lists of students in the selected classes after completion of school-level sampling.

 

Component 3. Preparation of national assessment instruments and context questionnaires

Purpose of the component

This component is aimed at preparing national versions of the assessment instruments, namely computer and information literacy and computational thinking task modules, through translation, linguistic adaptation and layout verification, as well as preparing context questionnaires for students, teachers, school principals and persons responsible for the school's digital development through translation, linguistic and structural adaptation, and layout verification.

 

Scope of work

Under this component, the Consultant shall perform the following tasks.

3.1. Organisation of work on the preparation of national study instruments

The Consultant shall:

  • Analyse a step-by-step schedule for preparing the national versions of the study instruments submitted by the Client to the IEA International Study Center (Timeline Estimator), and ensure the completion of the translation, adaptation, verification, layout review and finalisation process according to the plan.
  • Participate in a Q&A session on the StudyExpert platform, through which the national versions of the study instruments will be prepared.

 

3.2. Preparation of national versions of the assessment instruments

 

Indicative volume: at least 5 computer and information literacy task modules and at least 6 computational thinking task modules, with an indicative minimum of 8 items per module, including one open-ended item.

 

The Consultant shall:

  • translate the assessment instruments into Ukrainian, ensuring substantive, terminological and functional equivalence with the source versions;
  • carry out linguistic adaptation of the assessment instruments to the Ukrainian context, including mandatory adaptation of elements marked in square brackets in the source materials and additional adaptation of individual elements initiated subject to agreement with the Client;
  • prepare the national versions of the assessment instruments for verification of translation quality and linguistic adaptation on the StudyExpert platform;
  • address comments and recommendations received following the verification of translation and linguistic adaptation and make the necessary changes to the national versions of the instruments;
  • review the layouts of the assessment instruments, including checking the correct display of text, graphic elements, formatting, numbering, instructions and response options.

 

3.3. Preparation of national versions of context questionnaires for the field trial

 

Indicative volume of materials to be prepared: Student Questionnaire — approximately 5,974 words; School Principal Questionnaire — approximately 5,650 words; Teacher Questionnaire — approximately 5,744 words; Digital technologies Coordinator Questionnaire (person responsible for the digital development of the educational institution) — approximately 3,324 words. The permissible indicative variation in word count is +/- 1%.

 

The Consultant shall:

  • translate the context questionnaires into Ukrainian, ensuring substantive, terminological and functional equivalence with the source versions;
  • linguistically adapt wording, terminology, instructions, categories and response options to the Ukrainian education context;
  • identify and justify the necessary structural adaptations to the context questionnaires, including adding, splitting or removing response categories; adding national thematic blocks or dimensions; adding national questions; and excluding from national administration particular international questions or thematic blocks, including those designated as international options. National thematic blocks and national questions shall be defined in consultation with the Client, the NIO, other institutions as designated by the Client, including UCEQA, SSEQU, etc.,  and shall cover, in particular: the implementation of the State Standard for Basic Secondary Education (competence-based learning outcomes in the informatics and digital domain); teachers' participation in NUS professional development; the use of digital equipment supplied to schools under state programmes and donor-funded projects, including LEARN; and school-level conditions for the development of information and communication competence. The number and wording of national additions shall respect the limits set by the IEA International Study Center.
  • ensure that structural and linguistic adaptations are entered, agreed and documented on the StudyExpert platform;
  • prepare the national versions of the context questionnaires for verification of structural adaptations, translation quality and linguistic adaptation;
  • address comments from the IEA International Study Center received following the verification of structural adaptations, translation and linguistic adaptation, and make the necessary changes;
  • verify the layouts of the context questionnaires, including their structure, routing logic, numbering, formatting, and the correct display of text, instructions and response options.

 

Component 4. Methodological and technical preparation for data collection

Purpose of the component

This component is aimed at ensuring the technical feasibility of conducting the field trial in the selected educational institutions, engaging Test Administrators and national quality assurance monitors, preparing manuals and methodological materials, and delivering training for School Coordinators, Test Administrators, national quality assurance monitors and other persons involved.

 

Scope of work

Under this component, the Consultant shall perform the following tasks.

4.1. Preparation of manuals and methodological materials, participation in training activities and delivery of trainings

  • Review training materials      on field operations, provided by the IEA International Study Center and brief the project team on the relevant procedures;
  • ensure the appointment of Test Administrators and, where necessary, determine the procedure for remuneration of their engagement (in coordination with the Client and other institutions as designated by the Client, including UCEQA, SSEQU, etc.);
  • engage national quality assurance monitors to cover 10% of the educational institutions selected for the study, including observing assessment sessions, interviewing School Coordinators and Test Administrators, and submitting observation results to the National Study Center, and determine the procedure for remuneration of their engagement;
  • translate and adapt national manuals and methodological materials, including the School Coordinator Manual, Test Administrator Manual, and materials for national quality assurance monitors;
  • agree with the IEA International Study Center on arrangements for pausing the assessment timer and prepare practical procedures for action in the event of an air-raid alert, evacuation, connectivity outage or other emergency;
  • deliver training for Test Administrators and, where necessary, School Coordinators;
  • ensure the allocation of digital content groups and generation of identifiers and passwords for access to StudyExpert for students, teachers, school principals and persons responsible for the digital development of educational institutions to complete the assessments and questionnaires, and provide all necessary information to Test Administrators and, where necessary, School Coordinators;
  • deliver training for national quality assurance monitors.

 

4.2. Ensuring the technical readiness of equipment

The Consultant shall:

  • organise checks of the compatibility of schools' computer equipment with the technical requirements of the software required for ICILS 2028;
  • ensure testing of access to the web-based version of StudyExpert on the equipment to be used for the assessment;
  • ensure the identification and documentation of technical issues that could impede assessment administration and coordinate measures to resolve them;
  • prepare recommendations for educational institutions on configuring computers, browsers, network connections and other necessary equipment by translating and adapting the “Preparing Computers” instructions provided by the IEA International Study Center;
  • determine the need for backup equipment for the field trial and, in coordination with the Client, arrange delivery of backup computer equipment to educational institutions where necessary;
  • provide technical support to educational institutions before and during assessment administration.

 

Component 5. Organisation and implementation of data collection within the field trial

Purpose of the component

This component is aimed at ensuring data collection (assessment and questionnaire administration) in the selected educational institutions in compliance with the procedures, timelines and assessment conditions established by the IEA International Study Center, as well as monitoring study participation in OSE.

 

Scope of work

Under this component, the Consultant shall perform the following tasks.

5.1. Administration of assessments and questionnaires

The Consultant shall:

  • develop and agree a schedule for conducting the field trial in the selected educational institutions;
  • ensure the organisation and administration of assessments and questionnaires in the selected educational institutions (in coordination with the Client and other institutions as designated by the Client, including UCEQA, SSEQU, etc.);
  • ensure compliance with the assessment procedures, timelines and conditions established by IEA;
  • ensure study quality monitoring in 10% of participating educational institutions, including observation of assessment sessions and interviews with School Coordinators and Test Administrators (in coordination with the Client and other institutions as designated by the Client, including UCEQA, SSEQU, etc.);
  • monitor the progress of data collection using OSE, StudyExpert, the ICILS Dashboard and other systems in accordance with the requirements of the IEA International Study Center;
  • ensure prompt response to organisational and technical issues that may arise during study administration;
  • ensure documentation of non-standard situations, procedural violations and technical incidents.

5.2. Collection and entry of student and teacher participation information

The Consultant shall:

  • after completion of the assessments and questionnaires, obtain from educational institutions information on the participation status of each selected student and teacher and verify the completeness, accuracy and consistency of the information received;
  • ensure that reasons for student and teacher non-participation are established where required by the study procedures;
  • enter information on student and teacher participation status into OSE;
  • ensure timely correction of identified errors and resolution of discrepancies in participation data;
  • monitor completeness of data entry until the end of the data collection phase.

 

Component 6. Processing of data collected during the field trial and transmission of data to the IEA International Study Center

Purpose of the component

This component is aimed at processing the collected data, including scoring responses to open-ended questions, coding information on parents' occupations, preparing the Survey Activities Questionnaire and transmitting all information to the IEA International Study Center, as well as subsequent interaction during processing of the field trial results.

 

Scope of work

Under this component, the Consultant shall perform the following tasks.

 

6.1. Scoring and coding

The Consultant shall:

  • participate, with 1–2 representatives, in the training organised by the IEA International Study Center in Brussels on 8–12 March 2027;
  • translate and adapt the guidelines for scorers and coders;
  • engage specialists to score students' responses to open-ended items and code information on parents' occupations with an estimated workload of 50 person-days, and determine the procedure for remuneration of their engagement;
  • organise and deliver training for scorers based on ICILS 2028 guidelines and materials;
  • organise and deliver training for coders on classifying and coding parents' occupations;
  • provide the engaged specialists with the necessary instructions, guidelines, examples and forms;
  • ensure that the engaged specialists score students' responses to open-ended items in accordance with the international scoring guidelines provided by IEA, following scoring quality control procedures, including double-scoring protocols;
  • ensure that coders code all students' responses concerning their parents' occupations or jobs in accordance with the international classification and coding guidelines.

 

6.2. Data submission and further interaction with the IEA International Study Center regarding processing of the field trial results

The Consultant shall:

  • Complete the Survey Activities Questionnaire, taking into account reports from national quality assurance monitors;
  • transmit to the IEA International Study Center, within the agreed timeframe and through the relevant systems, the complete set of field-trial data, participation data, scoring/coding results and required documentation;
  • coordinate interaction with the IEA International Study Center during data processing and respond to requests concerning data, documentation or operational matters.

 

6.3. Ensuring Preparedness for the ICILS 2028 Main Survey

The Consultant shall:

  • ensure methodological and organisational continuity between the field trial and the main survey by systematically documenting experience gained, challenges encountered, and solutions developed during the field trial;
  • identify methodological, organisational, and technical gaps and risks, and develop recommendations for addressing them in preparation for the main survey, particularly regarding sampling, school recruitment, personnel training, data collection and processing, quality assurance, and contingency planning, in accordance with IEA standards and procedures;
  • provide the Client with all relevant documentation, materials, and recommendations to preserve institutional knowledge and facilitate a seamless transition between the field trial and the main survey.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS)

 

Country: Lebanon

Project Name: Digital Skilling for Employment (DSE) Project

Grant / Trust Fund Nos.: MDTF-FD Grant No. TF0D1059 & JSDF Grant No. TF0D1200

Assignment Title: Employability & Career Readiness Trainer 

 

STEP Activity Reference No.: # 571887

 

1. Background & Context

The Digital Opportunity Trust (DOT Lebanon) has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (the World Bank), acting as administrator of the Japan Social Development Fund (JSDF Grant No. TF0D1200) and the Dutch PROSPECTS Fund (MDTF-FD Grant No. TF0D1059), toward the cost of the Digital Skilling for Employment (DSE) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The DSE Project aims to equip vulnerable youth and women across Lebanon with market-relevant digital skills and link them to real income-generating opportunities. Under Component 2: Productive Inclusion in the Digital Economy (Microwork)—specifically Subcomponent 2.2 (JSDF and PROSPECTS Package of Services for Microwork Inclusion)—DOT Lebanon delivers digital, technical, and soft skills training paired with coaching and direct linkage to online microwork opportunities.

 

2. Objective & Scope of the Assignment

DOT Lebanon is seeking a qualified Individual Consultant to serve as Employability & Career Readiness Trainers, reporting directly to Area Managers. The Trainers will complement the project's technical digital skills and microwork training by delivering practical, participatory, and youth-centered training that strengthens participants' workplace readiness, communication, professionalism, self-management, and job-search capabilities.

 

Key parameters and responsibilities of the assignment include:

 

  • Training Delivery & Curriculum: Deliver structured in-person sessions using DOT Lebanon-approved curriculum, training materials, and assessment tools covering CV and cover letter writing, interview preparation, workplace communication, teamwork, problem-solving, time management, adaptability, professionalism, self-development, self-esteem, confidence building, and motivation.
  • Cohort Structure & Coverage: The overall assignment covers 74 training groups across Lebanon (approximately 25 participants per group), distributed among 4 Trainers according to the DSE implementation schedule. Each cohort receives 18 hours of employability and career readiness training delivered over 6 sessions of 3 hours each.
  • Safeguarding & Field Coordination: Maintain a safe, inclusive learning environment in compliance with DOT Lebanon safeguarding, child protection, and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) standards (including mandatory PSEA training and certification), while coordinating closely with Area Managers and Field Officers on scheduling, logistics, and participant engagement.
  • Documentation & Reporting: Maintain verified attendance records and session logs, administer approved assessments and practical exercises, submit monthly timesheets and invoices by the 25th of each month, and submit a cohort completion report upon finishing each assigned cohort.
  • Duration & Level of Effort (LoE): The assignment will run from the date of contract signature until December 31, 2027. Each Trainer is contracted on an hourly basis at $20 per hour, up to a maximum contract ceiling of $10,080 (an indicative LoE of up to approximately 504 total working hours, averaging 15 to 35 hours per month depending on cohort schedules).

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be requested via email at procurementlb@dotrust.org.

 

3. Required Qualifications & Shortlisting Criteria

DOT Lebanon now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants must provide information (an updated Curriculum Vitae and supporting documentation) demonstrating that they meet the following qualifications and evaluation criteria:

 

  1. Educational Background:
    • Bachelor's degree in Education, Business Administration, Social Sciences, Human Resources, or a related field relevant to employability and career readiness training.
    • Recognized professional certification(s) in training, facilitation, coaching, career guidance, or human resources will be considered an advantage.
  2. Relevant Professional Experience:
    • Minimum of five (5) years of demonstrated experience delivering employability, career readiness, soft skills, life skills, or related training.
    • Demonstrated track record delivering training on CV and cover letter writing, interview preparation, workplace communication, teamwork, problem-solving, time management, and professionalism.
    • Proven experience coaching, mentoring, or providing structured feedback to youth and adults, preferably within employability, workforce development, NGO/INGO, or development programs.
  3. Facilitation, Organizational & Digital Competencies:
    • Strong facilitation, presentation, classroom management, and participatory/experiential learning skills, with the ability to adapt delivery methods to diverse learner needs while adhering to approved curricula.
    • Basic digital literacy and proficiency in Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms) for training delivery and documentation.
    • Ability to travel and deliver in-person training sessions across assigned regions in Lebanon.
  4. Language Proficiency:
    • Full professional fluency in English and Arabic (written and spoken) is required.
    • Knowledge of French is considered an asset.

 

4. Conflict of Interest, Integrity & Audit Requirements

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023, and February 2025) ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

 

In addition, all selected Consultants must:

 

  • Have no actual or potential conflict of interest, including any close business or family relationship with professional staff of DOT Lebanon, any project implementing partner, or any party involved in preparing the TOR, the selection process, contract signing, or contract supervision.
  • Not have engaged in corrupt, fraudulent, collusive, coercive, or obstructive practices in competing for or executing the contract.
  • Permit the World Bank and/or auditors appointed by the World Bank to inspect and audit all accounts, records, and documents relating to the application and performance of the contract.

 

5. Selection Method

The  Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in Section VII (paragraphs 7.34–7.39) of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. Interested candidates will be evaluated and ranked based on their qualifications, relevant experience, and capability to carry out the assignment as demonstrated in their submitted CVs and supporting documents.

 

6. Submission Instructions & Equal Opportunity Notice

Further information can be obtained via email at procurementlb@dotrust.org during office hours (09:00 to 17:00).

 

Expressions of Interest—comprising an updated Curriculum Vitae (CV), a signed Expression of Interest & Conflict of Interest Declaration Form (Annex below), and copies of relevant academic degrees/certifications—must be sent by email to procurementlb@dotrust.org with the subject line "REOI – Employability & Career Readiness Trainer (DSE Project) no later than 9 December 2026 at 15:00 hours.


 

DOT Lebanon enforces a zero-tolerance policy toward all forms of discrimination, harassment, and bullying, and values diversity and equal employment opportunities regardless of race, gender, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, disability, age, language, or social origin. Women, persons with disabilities, and candidates from diverse backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.

The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (the Bank), acting as the administrator of the JSDF Fund and the Dutch PROSPECTS Fund, has agreed to provide financing for the Project, as set out in the Agreement.

The assignment falls under Component 2: Productive Inclusion in the Digital Economy (Microwork), which prepares vulnerable youth to participate in microwork opportunities through practical skills, mentorship, and access to freelance opportunities. DOT Lebanon is responsible for implementing Component 2.

Under Component 2, Subcomponent 2.1: Supply and Demand Assessment includes the assessment of youth baseline skills and constraints, local, regional, and global microwork demand, potential digital employment sectors, and clients and microwork platforms for partnership and micro-job creation. Subcomponent 2.2: JSDF and PROSPECTS Package of Services for Microwork Inclusion includes digital, technical and soft skills training, coaching and support to complete microtasks, profile creation on microwork platforms, and linkage to microwork opportunities.

 

  1. General Introduction & Grant Description: 

 

Lebanon continues to face one of the world’s most severe economic and financial crises, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Port of Beirut explosion, and the 2023-2024 conflict. These consecutive shocks have severely weakened labor market prospects, increased unemployment, and expanded poverty. Traditional employment pathways are increasingly constrained due to business closures, limited job creation, and instability.

 

At the same time, digital transformation and remote gig work are reshaping global labor markets. Microwork, small, simple digital tasks such as data tagging, transcription, verification, or AI data labeling, offers accessible, flexible income opportunities for individuals with basic digital literacy. Its low entry barriers make it particularly suitable for poor and vulnerable youth, women, and refugees.

 

The DSE project  aims to equip youth and women with market-relevant digital skills and linking them to real income-generating opportunities, the Project supports Lebanon’s recovery from different crises while advancing WBG MENA strategies on human capital, economic inclusion, gender equality, and a resilient, future-ready workforce.

 

Under the DSE project, the Digital Skills for Employment (DSE) builds on global experiences in Economic Inclusion (EI) programs and adapts them to a digital context, replacing traditional asset transfers with tablets or smartphones and pairing skills training with coaching and direct linkage to online income opportunities.





 

  1. Objective and Scope of work: 

 

The Employability & Career Readiness Trainers under the Digital Skills for Employment (DSE) Project are responsible for delivering high-quality, inclusive, and youth-centered training focused on employability, career readiness, and personal development. Microwork is a central pathway under DSE, providing participants with an accessible entry point to online income-generating opportunities. The Employability & Career Readiness Trainer complements the technical digital skills and microwork training delivered under the Project by strengthening participants’ workplace readiness, communication, professionalism, self-management, job-search skills, and ability to effectively pursue digital work and income-generating opportunities.

 

The trainers will deliver assigned structured sessions covering CV and cover letter writing, interview preparation, workplace communication, teamwork, problem-solving, time management, adaptability, professionalism, self-development, self-esteem, confidence building, motivation, and other relevant life and employability skills. DOT Lebanon will provide the approved curriculum, training materials, learning resources, and assessment tools. Trainers are responsible for delivery and are not expected to develop or revise the curriculum or training content. They may adapt facilitation techniques and delivery methodologies to participants’ learning needs, but any substantive modification to the approved content requires prior approval from DOT Lebanon. Training should be practical, participatory, and aligned with the needs of participants and the objectives of the DSE Project.

 

The Employability & Career Readiness Trainers will also ensure a safe and inclusive learning environment in line with DOT Lebanon safeguarding standards. They will be trained and certified on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) by the PSEA Focal Point and are required to comply with all safeguarding, child protection, and ethical conduct policies. They will coordinate closely with Area Managers and Field Officers to ensure smooth implementation, participant engagement, and effective monitoring of training activities. The assignment covers 74 training groups in total, to be distributed among 4 Employability & Career Readiness Trainers according to the DSE implementation schedule. Each group is expected to include approximately 25 participants. Each cohort, under both JSDF and PROSPECTS, receives 18 hours of employability and career readiness training (6 sessions of 3 hours). Training will be delivered in person across Lebanon. The training schedule will be coordinated between the relevant Area Manager, Trainer, and participants. The actual number of cohorts, sessions, beneficiaries, locations, and monthly assignments allocated to each trainer will be determined by DOT Lebanon based on implementation needs and reflected in the approved assignment schedule.

The Employability & Career Readiness Trainer shall deliver assigned training sessions according to the agreed schedule and DOT Lebanon-approved curriculum and materials; maintain attendance records; administer and document approved assessments and practical exercises, as applicable; submit a timesheet monthly for payment purposes; and submit a simple cohort completion report upon completion of each assigned cohort.

The cohort completion report shall be submitted to the relevant Area Manager using a simple format provided or approved by DOT Lebanon and shall include, at a minimum, sessions delivered, attendance, assessment completion and results where applicable, key observations or challenges, and any required follow-up. The Digital Opportunity Trust (DOT Lebanon) (the Recipient) will implement the Digital Skilling for Employment (DSE) Project, as set out in the Grant Agreement (the Agreement). The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (the Bank), acting as the administrator of the JSDF Fund and the Dutch PROSPECTS Fund, has agreed to provide financing for the Project, as set out in the Agreement.

The assignment falls under Component 2: Productive Inclusion in the Digital Economy (Microwork), which prepares vulnerable youth to participate in microwork opportunities through practical skills, mentorship, and access to freelance opportunities. DOT Lebanon is responsible for implementing Component 2.

Under Component 2, Subcomponent 2.1: Supply and Demand Assessment includes the assessment of youth baseline skills and constraints, local, regional, and global microwork demand, potential digital employment sectors, and clients and microwork platforms for partnership and micro-job creation. Subcomponent 2.2: JSDF and PROSPECTS Package of Services for Microwork Inclusion includes digital, technical and soft skills training, coaching and support to complete microtasks, profile creation on microwork platforms, and linkage to microwork opportunities.

 

  1. General Introduction & Grant Description: 

 

Lebanon continues to face one of the world’s most severe economic and financial crises, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Port of Beirut explosion, and the 2023-2024 conflict. These consecutive shocks have severely weakened labor market prospects, increased unemployment, and expanded poverty. Traditional employment pathways are increasingly constrained due to business closures, limited job creation, and instability.

 

At the same time, digital transformation and remote gig work are reshaping global labor markets. Microwork, small, simple digital tasks such as data tagging, transcription, verification, or AI data labeling, offers accessible, flexible income opportunities for individuals with basic digital literacy. Its low entry barriers make it particularly suitable for poor and vulnerable youth, women, and refugees.

 

The DSE project  aims to equip youth and women with market-relevant digital skills and linking them to real income-generating opportunities, the Project supports Lebanon’s recovery from different crises while advancing WBG MENA strategies on human capital, economic inclusion, gender equality, and a resilient, future-ready workforce.

 

Under the DSE project, the Digital Skills for Employment (DSE) builds on global experiences in Economic Inclusion (EI) programs and adapts them to a digital context, replacing traditional asset transfers with tablets or smartphones and pairing skills training with coaching and direct linkage to online income opportunities.





 

  1. Objective and Scope of work: 

 

The Employability & Career Readiness Trainers under the Digital Skills for Employment (DSE) Project are responsible for delivering high-quality, inclusive, and youth-centered training focused on employability, career readiness, and personal development. Microwork is a central pathway under DSE, providing participants with an accessible entry point to online income-generating opportunities. The Employability & Career Readiness Trainer complements the technical digital skills and microwork training delivered under the Project by strengthening participants’ workplace readiness, communication, professionalism, self-management, job-search skills, and ability to effectively pursue digital work and income-generating opportunities.

 

The trainers will deliver assigned structured sessions covering CV and cover letter writing, interview preparation, workplace communication, teamwork, problem-solving, time management, adaptability, professionalism, self-development, self-esteem, confidence building, motivation, and other relevant life and employability skills. DOT Lebanon will provide the approved curriculum, training materials, learning resources, and assessment tools. Trainers are responsible for delivery and are not expected to develop or revise the curriculum or training content. They may adapt facilitation techniques and delivery methodologies to participants’ learning needs, but any substantive modification to the approved content requires prior approval from DOT Lebanon. Training should be practical, participatory, and aligned with the needs of participants and the objectives of the DSE Project.

 

The Employability & Career Readiness Trainers will also ensure a safe and inclusive learning environment in line with DOT Lebanon safeguarding standards. They will be trained and certified on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) by the PSEA Focal Point and are required to comply with all safeguarding, child protection, and ethical conduct policies. They will coordinate closely with Area Managers and Field Officers to ensure smooth implementation, participant engagement, and effective monitoring of training activities. The assignment covers 74 training groups in total, to be distributed among 4 Employability & Career Readiness Trainers according to the DSE implementation schedule. Each group is expected to include approximately 25 participants. Each cohort, under both JSDF and PROSPECTS, receives 18 hours of employability and career readiness training (6 sessions of 3 hours). Training will be delivered in person across Lebanon. The training schedule will be coordinated between the relevant Area Manager, Trainer, and participants. The actual number of cohorts, sessions, beneficiaries, locations, and monthly assignments allocated to each trainer will be determined by DOT Lebanon based on implementation needs and reflected in the approved assignment schedule.

 

  1. Expected Deliverables and Reporting:

The Employability & Career Readiness Trainer shall deliver assigned training sessions according to the agreed schedule and DOT Lebanon-approved curriculum and materials; maintain attendance records; administer and document approved assessments and practical exercises, as applicable; submit a timesheet monthly for payment purposes; and submit a simple cohort completion report upon completion of each assigned cohort.

The cohort completion report shall be submitted to the relevant Area Manager using a simple format provided or approved by DOT Lebanon and shall include, at a minimum, sessions delivered, attendance, assessment completion and results where applicable, key observations or challenges, and any required follow-up. Attendance records and session-level documentation shall be maintained and submitted in accordance with DOT Lebanon procedures.

Background

Services for the position of Advisor to Minister Youth and Sports are required by the Ministry of Youth and Sports (MoYS), Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) through Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs to support implementation of a World Bank-funded project, Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST You) (P507443). The selected candidate will be hired under the BOOST-YOU and will work for the government’s National Social Protection Program.

Project Overview

The Federal Government of Somalia, in partnership with the World Bank, is implementing the Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment in Somalia (BOOST-YOU) through the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs (MoLSA)’s Social Protection Platform known as “Baxnaano”. The program supports poor and vulnerable households through the following components:

Component 1: Connecting Youth and Women to Better Jobs Today: Supports 28,000 youth (60% women & 5% disable persons) in urban areas with limited job opportunities and prolonged periods of inactivity, benefit from economic inclusion activities (wage and self-employment activities). contributing directly creating jobs and strengthening households’ resilience.

Component 2: Investing in People for Better Jobs Tomorrow: The component will deliver regular cash transfers to 50,000 of the poorest households to meet basic needs, enhance climate-challenged food security, and prevent negative coping strategies during climate shocks, which in turn helps safeguard the human capital necessary for productive participation in the labor force. Approximately 10,000 shock affected poor and vulnerable households will be supported with emergency cash transfers as part of a contingent financing arrangement in case of climate shocks. 30,000 pregnant women and mothers with children under two will receive health- and nutrition-linked co-responsibility cash transfers (CCTs) to promote maternal and child health, reduce malnutrition, and improve early childhood development, strengthening the human capital necessary for future workforce productivity whilst mitigating adverse climate impacts. An education CCT program will target 5,000 children from the poorest and most climate-affected households, helping build the foundation required for long-term employability by increasing school enrollment and attendance.

Component 3: Adaptive Social Protection Systems and Project Management: Supports enhancement of an adaptive social protection system, the National Socio-Economic Survey and project management including institutional capacity building for MoLSA. The objective of this support is to create a robust, efficient, and responsive social protection infrastructure. By strengthening institutional capacity, enhancing data management, strengthening the delivery system and registering the population in the USR, this component lays the foundation for sustainable and effective social protection and multisectoral poverty targeted investments. Under this component National Socio-economic Survey (NSES) will register 12 million people in Somalia in the USR collecting socio-economic data to inform targeting for pro-poor programs in the country. The component also provides support for effective project management, capacity building and oversight of project activities.

The Ministry is seeking to hire the Advisor to the Minister Youth & Sports who will provide comprehensive policy advice to the Ministry’s leadership, departmental units, programs, and project teams as required.

 

Scope of the position

The Advisor to the Minister shall provide strategic policy and technical advice to the Minister of Youth and Sports on the formulation, implementation, coordination, and monitoring of youth development policies, programs and initiatives. The Advisor will support the Ministry in promoting youth empowerment, social inclusion, employment, psychosocial well-being, gender-responsive programming and protection of vulnerable youth, while strengthening collaboration with government institutions, development partners, civil society organizations, and the private sector to improve opportunities and outcomes for young people across Somalia.

Objectives 

The objective of the position is to provide strategic advice and technical support in the formulation of policies, development of programs and projects, and coordination of national and international initiatives related to labor and social affairs.

Duties and Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the Advisor include the following:

 

  • Provide strategic policy advice to the Minister on youth development, employment, entrepreneurship, social inclusion, mental health, sports development, and human capital initiatives.
  • Lead the development, review and implementation of national policies, strategies, frameworks, action plans, and recommendations aimed at improving the socio-economic well-being of young people in Somalia.
  • Advise the Minister on emerging national and international trends, evidence and best practices related to youth development and recommend policy reforms to strengthen government programmes.
  • Coordinate with relevant ministries, including the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Women and Human Rights Development, Federal Member States, and development partners to promote integrated youth development initiatives.
  • Develop policy recommendations and programme concepts that improve access to education, skills development, employment opportunities, entrepreneurship and social protection for youth.
  • Lead initiatives to strengthen labour market participation of young people by facilitating partnerships with public institutions, private sector employers, vocational training providers, and development partners.
  • Design and promote programmes that support youth employability, career guidance, internships, apprenticeships, business incubation, entrepreneurship, and access to decent work.
  • Develop strategies and coordination mechanisms to improve labour market inclusion of youth with disabilities by facilitating access to vocational training, workplace accommodations, employment services, assistive technologies, and employer engagement initiatives.
  • Provide strategic guidance on designing and implementing inclusive programmes that promote equal opportunities for women, persons with disabilities, internally displaced youth, and other marginalized groups.
  • Lead the development of initiatives to establish and strengthen psychosocial support services for young people, including the recruitment, deployment and supervision of qualified counsellors to provide mental health and psychosocial support in youth centres, educational institutions and community settings.
  • Develop policies and operational guidelines for youth counselling services, including referral pathways for specialized mental health, protection, and social welfare services.
  • Promote youth resilience, conflict prevention, peacebuilding, social cohesion and violence prevention initiatives through evidence-based programmes and community engagement.
  • Support the establishment and operationalization of safe spaces for adolescent girls, ensuring that these facilities provide protection, life skills education, psychosocial support, reproductive health information, mentorship and opportunities for personal development.
  • Promote the establishment of youth-friendly community centres that provide integrated services, including counselling, career guidance, life skills development, recreational activities, digital learning opportunities and referral services.
  • Advise on the development of care facilities and integrated support services for vulnerable youth, including young women, youth with disabilities, survivors of violence, internally displaced youth and those requiring psychosocial, educational or livelihood support.
  • Facilitate partnerships with United Nations agencies, development partners, civil society organizations, academic institutions and the private sector to mobilize technical and financial resources for youth development programmes.
  • Review legislation, policies, and programme proposals affecting youth and provide recommendations to strengthen their effectiveness, inclusiveness and sustainability.
  • Commission and promote research, assessments and evidence generation on youth-related issues to inform policy formulation and programme design.
  • Monitor the implementation of youth policies, programmes and action plans and provide periodic policy advice to the Minister on implementation progress, emerging challenges, and recommended corrective measures.
  • Prepare policy briefs, cabinet submissions, speeches, technical papers, concept notes, briefing materials and presentations for the Minister on youth development issues.
  • Represent the Minister, when delegated, in national, regional and international meetings, conferences, technical forums, and consultations relating to youth development, employment, sports and human capital development.
  • Undertake visits to Federal Member States and project implementation areas to assess programme implementation, engage with youth organizations and local authorities, identify implementation challenges, and recommend practical measures for improving programme delivery.
  • Promote meaningful participation of youth in policy dialogue, governance processes and decision-making through consultations, forums and engagement platforms.
  • Support resource mobilization efforts through preparation of project proposals, investment cases, partnership frameworks and donor engagement strategies.
  • Ensure that youth programmes are gender-responsive, disability-inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and aligned with national development priorities and international commitments, including the Sustainable Development Goals.
  • Perform any other duties assigned by the Minister that are consistent with the objectives of the Ministry and the position.

 

    1. Key Deliverables

 

  • National youth policy recommendations and strategic advisory papers.
  • Youth development strategies, action plans, and implementation frameworks.
  • Framework for psychosocial support services for youth, including a plan for recruitment and deployment of counsellors.
  • Strategy for labour market inclusion of youth with disabilities.
  • Framework for establishing safe spaces for adolescent girls and integrated youth-friendly service centres.
  • Recommendations for youth employment, entrepreneurship, and skills development programmes.
  • Partnership and resource mobilization strategy for youth development initiatives.

 

  1. Qualifications

The Advisor must possess the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • Master’s degree in public policy, Public Administration, Development Studies, Economics, Social Sciences, Youth Development, International Development, or another relevant discipline. A PhD or equivalent professional qualification will be an added advantage.
  • At least ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in policy development, public sector reform, youth development, social protection, labor market programs or human capital development.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing national policies, strategies, and programmes related to youth, employment, social inclusion or human development.
  • Proven experience working with government institutions, international organizations, UN agencies, development partners, or large-scale donor-funded programs.
  • Strong understanding of Somalia's institutional framework, youth challenges, labour market dynamics, and national development priorities.
  •  
    1. Competence
  • Strong policy analysis and strategic planning skills.
  • Excellent communication, analytical, and interpersonal skills, and report writing skills.
  • Ability to coordinate multi-stakeholder initiatives.
  • Strong leadership and advisory capacity.
  • Knowledge of the youth, jobs and labor sectors in Somalia.
  • Fluency in English and Somali languages.

Reporting

The Advisor will report directly to the Minister of Youth and Sports, while also keeping the Baxnaano Program Manager and relevant units informed as needed.

Workstation

The Advisor will be based in Mogadishu and housed under the Ministry of Youth and Sports Head office.

Timeframe, Duration, and Commencement

The Advisor will be engaged for a period of 1 year with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance.

The  AD Elektrani na Severna Makedonija, vo drzhavna sopstvenost, Skopje (“Recipient”) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Bitola Gas-Fired Combined Heat and Power Plant and District Heating Network Expansion Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include preparation of the Feasibility studies for the development of the “Bitola Gas-Fired Combined Heat and Power (CHP) Plant and District Heating Network Expansion” Project. It is expected that the commencement of activities by the Consultants for all studies will be at the beginning of year 2027 and expected Completion: December 2027. The Consultant shall mobilize within fifteen (15) working days after Contract signing.

 The Activities for which the Grant is provided consist of the following parts:

  1. Technical and Economic Preparation

Carrying out pre-investment studies to confirm the feasibility of the Project including:

(i) a feasibility study and basic design for the Bitola gas-fired CHP plant and its gas pipeline connection (as well as associated facilities such as grid connection), including assessment of optimal capacity, technology options, fuel supply assumptions, heat offtake, and system integration. The feasibility study would assess use of existing infrastructure in Bitola;

(ii) a feasibility study and technical designs for the expansion of the Bitola district heating (DH) network, including demand assessment, network routing, phasing, and investment prioritization; and

 

  1. Environmental and Social Instruments Preparation

Undertaking environmental and social assessments and preparing Project’s environmental and social risks management instruments including Environmental and Social Impact Assessment(s) – ESIA(s) with embedded Environmental and Social Management Plan(s), Resettlement Policy Framework(s) - RPFs/Resettlement Action Plan(s) – RAPs, Labor Management Procedures (LMP) and Stakeholder Engagement Plan(s) – SEPs in accordance with the World Bank requirements. 

  1. Institutional and Capacity Building Support

Carrying out upstream preparatory work of institutional components of the Project, as well as related workshops and learning exchanges including:

  1. capacity building and training activities to enhance ESM’s capacity regarding preparation and implementation of large energy infrastructure projects, including project management, procurement planning, contract management, and environmental and social risks management;
  2. institutional strengthening to support financial planning, budgeting, and cost recovery related to CHP and district heating (DH) network investments, including tariff and cost-recovery considerations;
  3. support towards establishment and operationalization of Project implementation arrangements, including the working group, roles and responsibilities, and coordination mechanisms for the follow-on investment.
