APPEL À MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT

(SERVICES DE CONSULTANTS – SÉLECTION DE CABINETS)

Intitulé de la mission : « RECRUTEMENT D’UNE ASSISTANCE TECHNIQUE POUR L’AUTORITR DE RÉGULARITÉ DES SECTEURS DE L’EAU, DE L’ÉLECTRICITÉ ET DE L’EAU POTABLE (AREE) POUR UE FORMATION ET UN MENTORAT ENTRE PAIRS ».

 

Numéro de référence : GN-GWSP-573139-CS-QCBS

 

DÉBUT : 23/11/2026                                     FIN : 18/12/2026

 

 

  1. Contexte général

 

Le Gouvernement de la République de Guinée a obtenu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet Eau et Assainissement de Guinée (PEAG), et envisage d’utiliser une partie des fonds pour financer des services de consultants relatifs au recrutement d’une assistance technique pour l’Autorité de Régulation des Secteurs de l’Electricité et de l’Eau Potable (AREE) pour une formation et un mentorat entre pairs.

L’assistance technique est chargée d’appuyer l’AREE dans la mise en place d’un dispositif opérationnel, structuré et durable de régulation du secteur de l’eau potable, intégrant les dimensions institutionnelles, juridiques, économiques, techniques et financières. Sa mission contribuera également à l’élaboration d’une méthodologie tarifaire robuste et au renforcement durable des capacités de l’autorité de régulation. Il aura pour missions spécifiques de :

  • Réaliser un diagnostic institutionnel, juridique, économique, tarifaire, financier et technique du cadre de régulation du secteur de l’eau potable et des capacités de l’AREE ;
  • Élaborer un cadre structuré et opérationnel de régulation adapté au contexte institutionnel et sectoriel guinéen ;
  • Proposer un modèle durable de financement du régulateur permettant de renforcer progressivement son autonomie financière ;
  • Élaborer les instruments réglementaires, les outils opérationnels et les mécanismes de suivi nécessaires à l’exercice efficace des missions de régulation ;
  • Mettre en place un dispositif de suivi, de contrôle et d’évaluation des performances de l’opérateur historique ;
  • Développer un dispositif de régulation économique et tarifaire comprenant une méthodologie tarifaire, un modèle financier applicable au secteur, des mécanismes d’ajustement des tarifs et d’arbitrage entre les tarifs et les subventions requises ;
  • Renforcer les capacités techniques, institutionnelles et opérationnelles de l’AREE afin d’assurer l’appropriation durable des outils, procédures et mécanismes développés dans le cadre de la mission ;
  • Appuyer l’opérationnalisation progressive du dispositif de régulation du secteur de l’eau potable.

Les Termes de Références (TDRs) détaillés de la mission peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous : abayocoordonnateurpeag@gmail.com

L’Unité de Coordination du Projet Eau et Assainissement de Guinee (UC/PEAG)  invite les firmes de consultants éligibles (« Consultants ») à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution du Service (documentation en langue française).

La liste restreinte sera établie selon les critères suivants :

(i) Activités principales et le nombre d’années d’exercice

  • Justifier d’au moins dix (10) ans d’expériences dans la mise en place d’un cadre de régulation du secteur de l’eau assorti des principaux outils nécessaires à son opérationnalisation effective..

 (ii) Expérience requise (ou similaire) 

  • Avoir réalisé au moins ttrois (3)projets de régulation au cours des dix (10) dernières années.

                   

(iii) Capacité technique et administrative de l’entreprise (Agrément/ou organisation)

Le personnel clé ne sera pas évalué lors de l’établissement de la liste restreinte.

The Government of the Republic of Botswana, through the Ministry of Health, is implementing the Botswana Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Project with World Bank support under the regional Multiphase Programmatic Approach for Eastern and Southern Africa. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen health-system resilience and multisectoral preparedness and response to health emergencies. The project is structured around four components. Component 1 strengthens preparedness and resilience through improved governance and multisectoral coordination, access to quality health commodities, and health system digitalization. Component 2 improves detection and response capabilities. Component 3 supports project management, fiduciary oversight, and monitoring and evaluation. Component 4 is a Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) enabling rapid reallocation of funds in response to an eligible emergency. The survey forms part of the investments under Component 1, Sub-Component 1.3, which aims to strengthen the quality and utilization of data. Specifically, it falls under Sub-Activity 1.3.11.3.2 of the Project, which focuses on strengthening health information systems, improving data quality and promoting the use of evidence for planning and decision-making.

The MoH is seeking an individual Survey Coordinator to support the preparation, implementation, and completion of the Botswana MICS. The coordinator will provide technical advice and coordination support to the MoH and the survey implementing institution, including its sampling and data processing experts, throughout survey planning, questionnaire design, sampling, training, fieldwork, data processing, analysis, reporting, dissemination, and archiving, ensuring adherence to MICS protocols and recommendations.

A full ToRs is available at website www.bomra.co.bw

  • Demonstrated experience in questionnaire customization, ethical review, listing and mapping, training and field supervision visits, CAPI data collection, data processing and validation, analysis, and dissemination.
  • Strong computer skills and strong expertise in statistical analyses (familiarity with data processing and data analysis software, particularly SPSS),
  • Experience engaging/coordinating with National Statistics Organizations, Ministries of Health, and development partners.
  • Proven ability to manage work plans, budgets, risks, technical reviews, and follow-up actions,
  • Prior experience working with UNICEF MICS protocols and regional or global technical review processes would be highly desirable. .

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:

The Government of The Gambia in collaboration with The World Bank is implementing The Gambia Infrastructure Project (GIP) with the development objective to “increase resilient transport and energy access and strengthen institutional capacity in the provision of transport and energy services in The Gambia”. The project is to be financed by an International Development Association (IDA) Grant. The project aims to: (a) upgrade infrastructure access and network resilience through targeted investment in transport and energy investments in rural and urban areas; and (b) build capacity in the management of public service delivery by incorporating modern technologies and incentives for private sector participation.

Project Components

Component 1: Resilient Access to Infrastructure

Sub-Component 1.A: Last Mile Rural Connectivity.

Sub-Component 1.B: Résilient GBA Infrastructure.

Component 2: Policy, Planning and Management

Sub-Component 2.A: Sustainable Transport Policies and Road Sector Management

Sub-Component 2.B: Sustainable Energy Enabling Environment

Component 3: Service Delivery Modernization

Sub-Component 3.A: Motorization Management.

Sub-Component 3.B: Digitalization and Skills for Energy Services.

Component 4: Project Management and Capacity Building

Objective

The CPCU of the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs is responsible for monitoring GIP through periodic reports that track inputs, disbursement of funds and achievement of the indicators in the Results Framework, and it implements other projects funded by development partners with their own results and reporting requirements. Reliable and timely results data across this portfolio is essential for management decisions, accountability and learning. 

To this end, the CPCU is seeking the services of a Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer. The position will be recruited and financed under GIP, under Component 4.1 (Project Management), and will also support the M&E needs of other CPCU projects as needed. 

In detail, the scope of work of the M&E Officer shall include but not be limited to the following:

  • M&E Systems and Tools
  • Data Collection and Quality 
  • Analysis and Reporting
  • Field Monitoring and Beneficiary Feedback
  • Evaluation, Learning and Capacity Building

The Government of Mozambique (GoM) hereinafter referred to as “the Borrower” have received Advance funds from International Development Association (IDA) towards the costs of the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project, Preparation Phase. The funds have been channeled through the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project Office (GMNK) as the Project Implementation Agency, and GMNK intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for providing Project Advisory for undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. qualification, experience and skills in providing Project advisory services for reviewing the hydrological studies of hydropower projects;
  2. a minimum of Post Graduate Degree in the relevant hydrological disciplines and must have at least 15 years of professional experience relevant to the assignment.
  3. description of similar assignments previously carried out - must have done at least two (2) similar assignments (hydrological of hydropower advisory services), and
  4. experience of working in Sub-Sahara Africa - at least one (1) of the assignments should be in Sub-Shara Africa - and other regions.

 

Evidence shall be attached as supporting documents for the Expression of Interest.

 

Objective

 

The Project is being prepared for seeking financial support of the World Bank (the “Bank”) and therefore must comply with the World Bank Safeguards Policies and Performance Standards (see the concept project information document stage at the WB website [1]).  Accordingly, the Mphanda Nkuwa Project needs to comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) – Community Health and Safety (ESS4[2]). The hydrologist will:

 

  1. Review of the hydrological studies pertaining to the long-term inflow to the reservoirs, and spillway and diversion design floods with reference to international criteria. Assess the adequacy of spillway and diversion facilities, also considering increasing hydrological variability associated with global warming. Review of soil erosion data and estimate of sediment yield into the reservoirs, estimated reservoir sedimentation, and assessment of the long-term sustainable capacity that could be maintained by implementing appropriate management strategies. Review of layouts related to sediment management of the reservoirs including sediment flushing.
  2. Review of the design of spillway and tailrace facilities including flow conditions, energy dissipation and need for hydraulic modelling.
  3. Review of the designs of the diversion works, schedule and risk factors associated with diversion during construction and with the closure of diversion works at initial reservoir filling.

The assignment is for a period of six (6) years, covering project preparation, construction, and initial reservoir filling.
